title: Historical OHLCV backfill: paged klines, local cache and rate-limit-safe paging
body:
## Context
Implements **US-MKT-008** (Must): historical bars loaded on chart open, so a chart is useful immediately rather than after hours of recording. This is what makes R1's charting alpha demonstrable at all. The exchange constrains the shape: `GET /v5/market/kline` returns at most **1 000 rows** per call, as a **list-of-lists in descending time order**, which the adapter reverses and pairs with `end = start + interval_ms*1000 - 1` (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §2 kline mapping).

## Scope / Deliverables
- `fetch_klines(symbol, interval, start, end, limit=1000)` on the Bybit adapter, with paging until the configured days-to-load is covered, respecting the 1 000-row limit and the shared per-UID token bucket.
- Normalisation to `KlineEvent`: `start`/`end` ms -> µs, `open/high/low/close` as `Decimal`, `volume`, `turnover`, `confirm -> confirmed` (only `confirmed` bars are cached as final).
- Local cache in QuestDB `klines` (`docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`) keyed by `(symbol, interval, start)`, with a coverage index so a request can compute exactly which ranges are missing and fetch **only the tail/holes**.
- `GET /market/klines` REST endpoint (`22-api-openapi.yaml`) serving cache-first with a `coverage` descriptor; progress reporting for a long backfill so the UI can show "loading older bars..." without blocking interaction.
- Rate-limit behaviour: on `10018` the backfill **backs off with jitter**, keeps the partial result usable, and resumes; it never fails the whole request because a later page was throttled.
- Resumability: an interrupted backfill resumes from its coverage index rather than restarting.
- Serves **SCR-151** empty-state pattern (CMP-001, CMP-019, CMP-021, CMP-026).

## Out of scope
- Building non-time bars (tick/volume/range/renko) from trades - **E12**.
- Rebuilding bars from the tape and the `metadata_version` rebuild pipeline - **E12**/**E16**.
- Chart rendering and the progressive-load UX - **E11**/**E12**.
- Long-horizon retention policy - **E16**.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Backfill
  Given I open BTCUSDT 5m
  Then bars are paged from the kline endpoint until the configured days-to-load is covered
  And progress is reported so the caller can show a loading indicator

Scenario: Cache hit
  Given those bars are already stored
  Then they load from local storage in under 300 ms for 5000 bars and only the tail is fetched from the exchange

Scenario: Rate limited
  Given the exchange returns a rate-limit error mid-paging
  Then backfill backs off with jitter, the partial result stays usable
  And paging resumes without failing the overall request

Scenario: Descending payload is ordered correctly
  Given the exchange returns rows in descending time order
  Then the stored and returned series is ascending by start time with end = start + interval - 1 microsecond
  And no duplicate start timestamps exist across page boundaries

Scenario: Unconfirmed bar is not cached as final
  Given the newest returned row has confirm=false
  Then it is returned as an in-progress bar and is not written to the cache as a confirmed bar

Scenario: Interrupted backfill resumes
  Given the backend restarts while a 90-day backfill is in progress
  Then on the next request the coverage index shows the remaining holes and only those are fetched
```

## Technical notes / design
The coverage index is the core design: rather than tracking "how far back have we loaded", it stores contiguous covered ranges per `(symbol, interval)` so holes created by outages are first-class and fillable. Paging is sequential per symbol/interval to keep the token bucket predictable, with a bounded concurrency across symbols. Timestamps are microseconds; interval maths uses integer arithmetic only, never floats, so bar boundaries are exact.

## Test plan
Unit: page assembly, descending-to-ascending reversal, boundary maths, coverage-index merge/hole computation. Contract: recorded kline fixtures incl. a page boundary, an unconfirmed tail row and a `10018` response; OpenAPI contract test for `/market/klines`. Integration: cold backfill -> cache -> warm read asserting the 300 ms budget; restart-mid-backfill resume. Perf: 5 000-bar cache read p95; full 90-day 5m backfill wall time and request count.

## Security notes
Public data, unauthenticated. The endpoint's `start`/`end`/`limit` parameters are bounded server-side so an authenticated user cannot request an unbounded range and force a large exchange spend or a large database scan - an availability abuse case tested explicitly. Backfill work is queued and bounded per user.

## Accessibility notes
Progress is exposed as a numeric fraction plus a text status so SCR-151's empty state can announce "Loading older bars, 40% complete" via `aria-live` rather than only animating a spinner.

## Performance notes
Budgets (US-MKT-008 NFR): <=300 ms to first paint from cache for 5 000 bars; paging respects the 1 000-row limit; retries use jittered backoff; backfill never blocks the event loop or starves live ingestion (it uses a lower-priority bucket class than live-critical calls).

## Observability
`kline_backfill_pages_total{symbol,interval,result}`, `kline_backfill_duration_seconds`, `kline_cache_hit_ratio`, `kline_coverage_holes{symbol,interval}`, `bybit_rate_limited_total{code="10018",endpoint="kline"}`. Alert when a backfill has been retrying beyond a threshold.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario automated; QA black-box plan executed and signed off.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on the touched packages; contract tests green.
- [ ] Perf: 300 ms cache-read budget and backfill wall time recorded.
- [ ] Docs: `22-api-openapi.yaml` `/market/klines`, `21-database-schema.md` `klines` and `24-internal-schemas.md` kline mapping reconciled.
- [ ] Feature-flag state recorded (days-to-load default per environment).
- [ ] Demoed at Sprint Review on demo; PRs merged via merge queue with 2 approvals incl. code-owner.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E08-S01** (interval/symbol validity and precision), **E07** (QuestDB wiring). Blocks **E12** (series rendering needs history).

title: Build the SCR-100 watchlist panel and SCR-101 manager with live and stale states
body:
## Context
Implements the UI halves of **US-MKT-003** (Must: live columns, reorder and persist, and "Feed interrupted" greys cells "with a 'stale' marker rather than showing frozen values as if live") and the consumer side of **US-MKT-005**. It also hosts US-REC-002's SCR-100 indicator slot, which E16-S02 fills. The backend ticker work is done (E08-S03, #284). The server side of the `ticker` WS topic and the bulk snapshot are E08-T08, and `/watchlists` persistence is E08-T07; this story consumes both. `docs/design/E08/E08-D07.md` fixes the design: the 40-symbol cap is a security control (D07 §1, SR-073), and no per-tick logic goes into a statechart (`28-statechart-catalogue.md` §1.2). The risk retired here is a frozen price that looks live (`14-screens-catalogue.md` §0.5 item 4).

This story was filed from the planning gap that D07 C-5 (Q16), D05 Q8 and E08-S01's Out of scope all name: no backlog story built the SCR-100/101 UI. It takes the routes R-110 and R-111 from `apps/web/src/routes/manifest.ts`, which today lists them with `owner: "E13"` (the indicators epic); the manifest change belongs to this story's implementation. It builds the domain components it first needs (E05-S03 deferred CMP-055/056/067 "to the epic that first needs them").

## Scope / Deliverables
Every item cites its source.
- **SCR-100 pane** (pane kind `watchlist`, `14` SCR-100 "Route") in `apps/web/src/features/watchlist/`.
  - It is an ARIA grid: `role="grid"`, roving tabindex, caption, absolute `aria-rowcount` and `aria-rowindex`. CMP-049 gains an interactive grid mode (D07 D16, §5; `14` SCR-100 "A11y"). Rows are CMP-161 and list tabs are CMP-162.
  - Default columns are Symbol, Last, 24h %, Turnover USDT, Funding %, Funding in, OI Δ 24h %, Spread bps, Rec, and the fixed Status slot. Optional columns come from CMP-056 (D07 D8, §4.1).
  - Formatting follows D07 D9: tabular mono, `price_scale`, sign plus ▲/▼, U+2212, turnover to 3 significant figures, bps, and no colour on Last, Funding or Spread.
  - Compact (24 px) and comfortable (32 px) density, with the 200 % reflow to one card per symbol (D07 D30).
- **Live window** (D07 D6, D27, §4.6; `14` SCR-100 "Performance").
  - One batched `ticker` subscription carries at most 40 distinct symbols per connection, shared with other panes.
  - Window moves, list switches, adds and re-opens draw on the 5-per-60 s rebuild share. The client starts one only while fewer than 4 draws fall in the last 60 s, and moves are at least 2 s apart. Moves happen 300 ms after scroll settles.
  - A `sub` refused with `resync_rate_limited` shows "Live prices paused — retrying in 5 s" and backs off 5 s doubling to 60 s.
  - The footer count reads "120 symbols · 39 live" (D10). Updates are coalesced to 4 Hz, and the grid is virtualised beyond 60 rows.
  - Rows outside the window show "—" and "Not live" until E08-T08's bulk snapshot (D07 C-11) exists (D07 D7).
- **Data-confidence states** (D07 D1, D2, D4, D7, D17, D20, D21, D22, §4.2; `14` SCR-100 "States").
  - Ticker cells go stale at T1 = 5 s and escalate at T2 = 15 s. A stale row is a tint plus demoted text with the values kept, and one Status chip ("Stale 7s").
  - A stale OI Δ column carries a ⚠ on its header and one footer line.
  - Disconnected is a panel status, "Disconnected — last data 00:12 ago", for the whole outage. It is never a scrim and never gates a control (D07 §12 C-13 records the open E08-D11 difference, Q18).
  - A delisted row is struck through with a merged cell "Delisted by the exchange". Initialising and not-live states are each worded. The funding countdown runs on one shared 1 Hz clock (D22).
  - **The panel owns no live region.** It sends one polite summary to the app region on entering and one on leaving a stale episode, never per tick, row or age change (D17).
  - Staleness, coalescing and the clock are plain client code, not statecharts.
- **Interactions** (D07 §6, D5, D11, D36).
  - Activation sets the symbol of the pane's sync group through a port. The sync-group mechanism itself is E15-S04.
  - `Del` removes with Undo, and `Alt+↑/↓` reorders (§6.4).
  - "+ Add symbol" opens a non-modal CMP-017 popover with CMP-160, ranked by E08-S09's module. It stays open for several adds.
  - `Ctrl+F` filters. A live-column sort re-ranks at most every 2 s and holds while the pointer or focus is in the grid, shown as "Sort: 24h % ▾ · paused" plus "Re-sort".
  - The row menu (CMP-041) has Open in new chart, Send to panel ▸, Copy symbol, Move up/down, Remove, plus the record and unrecord items (slots; E16-S02 fills them).
  - Controls the session cannot use are E09-D09 T2, disabled with a reason and never hidden (D07 §6.6, §6.7, D13).
- **SCR-101 manager** (modal `?modal=watchlists`, R-110 opens it; D07 D24, §4.3, §4.4, §6.5; `14` SCR-101).
  - Create, rename (`F2`), duplicate and delete lists. Delete is a CMP-044 standard confirm with Cancel focused (D26).
  - Reorder symbols with move up/down buttons, `Alt+↑/↓` and drag. A move announces "BTCUSDT moved to position 2 of 12." (§6.4).
  - Bulk add by paste with a preview (D25).
  - Import and export as plain UTF-8 text, at most 64 KB, `.txt` or `.csv`. Unknown and delisted symbols are reported and never added (D14, §4.4).
  - Per-list columns.
  - Validation: names 1 to 80 characters, unique per user and checked client-side. At most 200 symbols per list, and at 200 the add control is T2 with "Watching 200 symbols — remove some to add more" (D10).
  - Each change applies locally, then `PUT /watchlists/{watchlistId}` replaces the list, and a failure rolls back with an inline error. The conflict state uses E08-T07's version field; until it lands the state is labelled "(contract pending)" (D15).
- **Routes:** R-110 and R-111 move to this story in `apps/web/src/routes/manifest.ts` (owner `E08`), and R-110 opens the SCR-101 modal (D07 D24).
- **Pane settings** `watchlist_id` and `watchlist_sort` (D35; the pane-settings owner is E15, D07 C-6).
- **Analytics** as listed in `14` SCR-100 and `14` SCR-101 "Analytics/audit", including `data_confidence.state_entered`.
- **Storybook** stories for each new or changed component: CMP-161, CMP-162, CMP-049 grid mode, CMP-056, CMP-067, CMP-239 compact form (D07 §5).
- **Fixtures:** recorded ticker fixture `ws/recorded_tickers_BTCUSDT.jsonl` and `instruments_after.json` (`packages/fixtures`). No invented payload shapes.
- **Open owner questions** D07 Q1 to Q18 stay at their defaults; this story builds the fallback each one names (D07 §12).

## Out of scope
- **A sparkline column** (D07 D33). The sparkline moves to SCR-104 (E08-S11).
- The `/watchlists` backend and migration (E08-T07); the `ticker` topic producer and the bulk snapshot (E08-T08); the `/market/open-interest` route (E24-T01, #665). Until they land the documented fallbacks apply: rows read "Not live", OI Δ reads "—".
- REC chip data and its 17 texts, and the Record and Keep-recording actions (E16-S02). The Rec cell renders nothing, or the restricted lock, while the recorder store is absent.
- Sync-group assignment UI (E15-S04) and the alert-creation flow (entry point only).
- Search ranking and the chooser submenu from SCR-102 ("Add to watchlist…" opens E08-S09's menu into this story's add path). Scanner "send matches to watchlist" is E08-S11.
- A default list (contract field missing, D07 C-3), optimistic-concurrency conflict resolution beyond E08-T07's version field (C-1), and the E08-D11 motion amendments pending Q18.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Live columns from one batched subscription
  Given a watchlist "Majors" with 12 symbols and the recorded ticker fixture replaying
  Then exactly one batched ticker subscription carries those 12 symbols
  And the grid exposes role="grid" with every header and cell readable by accessible name
  And cells repaint at no more than 4 Hz and no per-tick change is announced

Scenario: Stale rows are never presented as live
  Given SOLUSDT receives no ticker frame for 6 seconds
  Then its row shows the stale tint, demoted text, the kept values and a "Stale 6s" status chip
  And the stale state is carried by text as well as tone
  And exactly one polite summary is announced on entering the stale episode and one on leaving it

Scenario: Disconnected is a panel status, not a frozen price
  Given the transport drops with last data 12 seconds ago
  Then the panel header reads "Disconnected — last data 00:12 ago" and every row is demoted
  And SCR-152 announces the disconnect once and the panel does not repeat it
  And no control is blocked by the disconnect

Scenario: The 40-symbol cap and the live window hold
  Given a 120-symbol list and another pane holding one symbol that is not on the list
  Then 39 symbols are subscribed and rows in view outside them read "—" and "Not live"
  And the footer reads "120 symbols · 39 live"
  And no more than 4 window moves start in any 60 seconds
  Given a list holding 200 symbols
  Then the add control is disabled with "Watching 200 symbols — remove some to add more" before any attempt

Scenario: Reorder by keyboard persists, and a failed save rolls back
  Given SCR-101 is open on "Majors" and focus is on BTCUSDT
  When the user presses Alt+Down
  Then "BTCUSDT moved to position 2 of 12." is announced and the new order is saved with PUT /watchlists/{id}
  And the order is the same after a reload
  Given the save fails
  Then the order rolls back and an inline error with Retry is shown
  And axe reports zero serious or critical violations on SCR-100 and SCR-101 in both themes
```

## Technical notes / design
Estimate 8 is the ceiling and deliberately honest. Comparables are E21-S01 (8: live ladder grid) and E18-S01 (8); E10-S01 and E16-S01 are 5. It carries an ARIA grid, a subscription-window controller with a rate limit, eight data-confidence states, and a second surface (SCR-101). **If planning poker lands above 8, split along the surfaces:** S08a is the SCR-100 panel and S08b is the SCR-101 manager with import and export. Ticker values flow transport → observable → coalesced (4 Hz) → atom (Jotai); the window controller and the stale clock are plain modules with fake-clock unit tests.

## Test plan
Unit: window controller (40-symbol cap, rebuild share, 2 s spacing, back-off), stale thresholds T1/T2 on a fake clock, formatting (D07 D9), import parser (64 KB, unknown and delisted symbols). Component (RTL): grid roles and keyboard map, Status chip text, the one-summary announcement rule, SCR-101 reorder and rollback. E2E: QA plan cases E08-TC-C05 to C07 extended for SCR-100 and SCR-101. axe in both themes.

## Security notes
The 40-symbol cap per connection is a security control (D07 §1, SR-073): never exceeded and never bypassed with a second connection. Import accepts plain text only, at most 64 KB, and symbols are validated against the catalogue before any request. RBAC is server-side; the UI shows T2 reasons and never hides a control (E09-D09 A-6).

## Accessibility notes
ARIA grid with roving tabindex and absolute row indices; stale and disconnected states are carried by text as well as tone; the panel owns no live region and sends one polite summary per stale episode (D17); reorder announces the new position; 200 % reflow to cards (D30). axe zero serious or critical in both themes; keyboard-only path and a screen-reader spot-check recorded.

## Performance notes
Message to pixels under 100 ms p95 (`06-performance-and-load-standard.md`, D07 D32); repaint coalesced to 4 Hz; virtualised beyond 60 rows; no per-tick React state.

## Observability
Analytics events from `14` SCR-100 and SCR-101 "Analytics/audit", including `data_confidence.state_entered`; window rebuilds and `resync_rate_limited` refusals are counted client-side.

title: Build SCR-102 symbol search and the SCR-041 quick-switcher on one ranking rule
body:
## Context
Implements **US-MKT-002** (Must: ≤50 ms from the local catalogue, full ARIA combobox) and the user-facing half of **US-MKT-001** (delisted symbols hidden from search). E08-S01 (#182) provides the catalogue and endpoint and deferred "Client-side search UI and ranking"; E12-S11 (#451) "consumes the selection event". This story is that UI, as designed in `docs/design/E08/E08-D05.md` (D05 Q8, §16). It builds the domain components it first needs (E05-S03's deferral).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Client instrument index** in `apps/web/src/features/symbol-search/`.
  - It loads `GET /instruments` (Trading only, paged, `limit` ≤ 500) at shell bootstrap and hourly, and normalises the match fields once (D05 §3, §5; `14` SCR-102 "Data").
  - It reads `meta.cache_age_s` and `stale_since`. A subscribed symbol's `instrument_revision` re-reads it. No request is made per keystroke.
  - A 503 means "the server is still loading", not a failure (D05 D-5, §6.2).
- **One ranking module** (D05 D-3, §4).
  - Query normalisation: trim, upper-case, drop spaces and `/ - _`, cap at 32 characters. Fields are the symbol and the base with a leading multiplier stripped.
  - Tiers T1 to T5, tie-breaks (favourite, recent, symbol ASCII; turnover only once D05 Q3's bulk source exists), at most 50 ranked results.
  - **The eleven worked vectors V1 to V11 become the unit tests**: `btc`, `eth`, `btc/usdt`, `pepe`, `inch`, `sol`, `slu`, `luna`, `xyzzy`, `usdt` and empty.
  - It is the single source for SCR-102, SCR-041 and the palette's symbol group. SCR-012's own wiring stays with E10 and E49.
- **SCR-102 modal** (D05 §6, §8, §9; `14` SCR-102).
  - Anatomy per §6.1 and the target chip per D-10.
  - Windowed list per §5: at most 24 option nodes, keystroke to paint ≤ 50 ms, open ≤ 80 ms.
  - Combobox roles per §9.1: `aria-activedescendant`, an option holding text and chips only, no control inside an option.
  - Each state in the §6.2 copy deck, verbatim: idle, results, loading, load failed, refresh answered, refresh failed, stale, refreshing, checking a symbol, no matches, status rule, disconnected, armed target.
  - The symbol check for a settled no-match: one request, `^[A-Z0-9]{2,20}USDT$`, after a 300 ms rest, with "Check again" T2 for 60 s afterwards (§6.2, §12.2).
  - Delisted Recent rows: struck, "Delisted by the exchange", `aria-disabled`, not openable (§6.4, D-6).
  - Action menu (CMP-041, `Shift+F10` or Menu key or right-click or the detail bar's `⋯`): Open in target, Open in new chart, Open DOM ladder, Add to watchlist…, View symbol info, Remove from recent, with T2 and RBAC per §6.3.
  - Keyboard map per §8 and the keyboard-only path (flows F-1 and F-2).
  - Inert background: the TopBar and shell live regions sit outside the inert subtree (D-11, §9.2).
  - Commit announcements through the shell polite region (§6.2).
- **SCR-041 symbol half** (D05 §7; `14` SCR-041).
  - CMP-017 popover anchored to the toolbar symbol button, with a metadata preview: tick, lot, max leverage, funding, and 24 h turnover (or "—").
  - `Enter` commits the symbol and keeps the interval, `Shift+Enter` opens a new chart, `Esc` restores the current symbol, focus returns to the invoker. It never traps focus.
  - It emits the symbol-selection event that E12-S11 consumes.
  - A delisted current value reads "BTCUSDT is not trading on Bybit — choose another symbol."
- **24 h change and turnover** come only from tickers the client already holds, else "—". Search opens no subscription and makes no request (D-8).
- **Recents** (8) live for the session only. The Favourites group and its menu item are not rendered (D-9, the fallback for D05 Q6).
- **Open key `/`** is registered once E10-S02's dispatcher rule A-D05-2 exists. The fallback is `Ctrl+P` with a reviewed `reservedOverride` (D-1, D05 Q1). The owner's "Refresh from Bybit" (`POST /instruments/refresh` plus job polling) is T2 for other roles (§6.2).
- **Analytics** `symbol.searched`, `symbol.search_result_opened`, `empty_state_shown`, `chart.symbol_changed` (D05 §12.1). The query is never sent, only its length.
- **Storybook** for CMP-213, CMP-160, CMP-219 and CMP-026 variants (D05 §13).
- **Open owner questions** D05 Q1, Q2, Q3 and Q6 stay at their defaults; this story builds the fallbacks named above (Q1 `Ctrl+P` fallback, Q2 interval-strip slot only, Q3 "—" for 24 h values, Q6 session-only recents).

## Out of scope
- The interval strip and time-interval ladder (`1`–`9`, CMP-220, SCR-042) and the chart re-bind (E12-S11, E12-D09 NC-10). D05 D-12 and Q2 are open, so this story ships the symbol half and a slot only.
- Recording chips, the auto-record sentence data, "Record this symbol…" / M-023 (E16-S02). With the recorder store absent no chip renders.
- The SCR-103 drawer (E08-S10): this story's "View symbol info" item calls its `open(symbol, {source})` port, and the item appears once that port is registered.
- The watchlist chooser submenu behind "Add to watchlist…" (E08-S08, D07 D36).
- A favourites and recents store (D05 Q6), a bulk 24 h source (D05 Q3; E08-T08), server-side `?q=` per keystroke, and the SCR-012 palette itself.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fuzzy match is local and fast
  Given the instrument index holds a synthetic 500-instrument list marked as such
  When the user types "btc"
  Then BTCUSDT ranks first and no network request is made
  And keystroke to painted list is at most 50 ms at p95 and the dialog opens in at most 80 ms

Scenario: Keyboard-only selection and focus return
  Given focus is on a positions grid cell and no pointer is used
  When the user presses "/", types "eth", presses Down, then Enter
  Then the chart target switches to ETHUSDT, the dialog closes and focus returns to the grid cell
  And "Chart 1 now shows ETHUSDT, 1 minute." is announced once through the shell polite region
  And typing "btc/usdt", arrows and Esc in the field leaves the toast host empty

Scenario: No match is stated, never an empty list
  Given the catalogue is loaded
  When the user types "xyzzy"
  Then after a 300 ms rest one check of XYZZYUSDT returns 404
  And the CMP-026 state reads "No USDT perpetual matches 'xyzzy'." with "v1 supports Bybit USDT linear perpetuals only."
  Given the catalogue request answers 503
  Then the state reads "Loading the instrument list…" and never "no matches"

Scenario: A delisted recent is shown but cannot be opened
  Given LUNAUSDT (status Closed) is in Recent
  Then its row is struck through with "Delisted by the exchange" and is aria-disabled
  And Enter on it does nothing and the detail bar states why
  And no stale or disconnected marker appears on the row

Scenario: Stale catalogue and lost connection stay visible
  Given the catalogue meta reports stale_since 14 hours ago
  Then the footer shows the overdue notice and results remain usable
  Given the WebSocket disconnects while the dialog is open
  Then the footer reads "Disconnected — results come from the list loaded at 13:02 UTC." and opening is still allowed
  And 24 h cells read "—" rather than a frozen number
```

## Technical notes / design
Estimate 5, as E10-S01 (5: shell chrome) and E13-S01 (5: indicator picker with fuzzy search). The ranking is a pure module with eleven worked vectors; two surfaces share it; about thirteen catalogue states carry copy. Eight is the risk if the dispatcher work from E10-S02 slips into this story. The index normalises once at load; ranking runs synchronously on the main thread within the 50 ms budget.

## Test plan
Unit: ranking vectors V1 to V11, normalisation, the 50-result cap, the symbol-check regex and 300 ms rest on a fake clock. Component (RTL): combobox roles, every §6.2 state's copy, delisted Recent rows, focus return. E2E: QA plan cases E08-TC-A05 to A07. Perf: keystroke-to-paint p95 and open time on the synthetic 500-instrument list. axe in both themes.

## Security notes
Read-only market metadata. The symbol check sends only a value matching `^[A-Z0-9]{2,20}USDT$`; the typed query is never sent to analytics (length only). "Refresh from Bybit" is owner-only server-side; other roles see T2.

## Accessibility notes
Full ARIA combobox with `aria-activedescendant`, no control inside an option (axe `nested-interactive`), inert background with the shell live regions outside it, commit announcements through the shell polite region, focus returns to the invoker. axe zero serious or critical in both themes; keyboard-only path and a screen-reader spot-check recorded.

## Performance notes
Keystroke to painted list ≤ 50 ms p95, open ≤ 80 ms, at most 24 option nodes (D05 §5); no request per keystroke.

## Observability
`symbol.searched`, `symbol.search_result_opened`, `empty_state_shown`, `chart.symbol_changed` (D05 §12.1), query length only.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario automated; vectors V1 to V11 pass as unit tests; keystroke-to-paint p95 and open time recorded against the budgets.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80%; axe-core zero serious or critical in both themes; keyboard-only path and a screen-reader spot-check recorded.
- [ ] Storybook states for the new components; copy matches the D05 §6.2 deck verbatim.
- [ ] Docs: `14` SCR-102 and SCR-041 updated where the build diverged.

Also consumes E17-T04 (#413, web WS client, Done), named here and not in the twin's `blocked_by` because the roadmap §11.1 edge runs E08 → E17. Blocks E08-S08 (add flow), E08-Q05 (#282) and E16-S02 (#566, recording dot on SCR-041).

Planned for Sprint 06 (2026-10-30 → 11-05). The backlog twin carries `Backlog` because Sprint 06 is at its 90-point capacity in `validate.py`.

title: Build the SCR-103 symbol info drawer: contract rules, live market, coverage
body:
## Context
Implements the UI of **US-MKT-001** (precision and funding rules visible) and **US-MKT-004** (the "rules are enforced by the exchange" presentation; the order-ticket snapping is E30). It also serves US-REC-006's coverage display. The drawer keeps three kinds of fact apart because they differ in trust: exchange rules, live values that can go stale, and CandleViewer's own recording facts (`docs/design/E08/E08-D06.md` §1, D-1). D06 Q8 asks which FE ticket builds it, and this is it. It builds the domain components it first needs (E05-S03's deferral).

**Not Ready until E08-D06 (#174) is Done** (design-ahead DoR, `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1): the D06 text is merged but its boards are pending.

**Boundary with E16-S02 (#566).** In the drawer's CandleViewer band, the **coverage and gaps rows** (D06 §4.3) are this story's. The **recording-state rows and the Owner rows** (first-recorded time, disk, retention, pin, and "Record this symbol…") are E16-S02's; this story renders their slot.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Drawer shell** (CMP-046 modal, right side, 480 CSS px, full height below the TopBar and the SCR-152 slot, focus trap, sticky header and footer; D06 D-14, §10; `14` SCR-103 "Type").
  - `open(symbol, {source, section?})` is the opener contract, with a single registered port that E08-S09, SCR-100's row menu and SCR-047 call.
  - A second `open()` in the same window replaces the first (D-16).
  - Deep link `?panel=symbol-info&symbol=` is proposed for `12` (A-9) and is not required here.
- **Three bands** in the fixed order Contract rules, Live market, Recording in CandleViewer. Each is a `section` with an `h3`, a source tag ("Set by Bybit", "Live from Bybit", "Recorded by CandleViewer") and an as-of line. The contract band opens with "These rules are enforced by the exchange. CandleViewer shows them and cannot change them." (D06 D-1, §3).
- **Contract band** from `GET /instruments/{symbol}` (D06 §4.1, §5, §11.1).
  - Rows: status, tick size, quantity step, min and max quantity, minimum order value, max leverage, funding interval ("can change"), risk-limit tiers, provenance "Rules revision 7 · checked 2 h ago" (D-2).
  - It paints from the client index within 100 ms when warm and requests once per open.
  - Numbers are decimal strings, positional, minimal exact form. The sentences and examples come from the order ticket's rule source (E08-S02, `policy.py`) through one shared formatter (D-6, CR-2/CR-3), with units in their own column.
  - Risk-limit tiers are a captioned table: 3 rows plus "Show all N tiers", at most 8 rows, then an inner scroll. `[]` reads "Risk-limit tiers: not available yet" (D-8).
  - An overdue catalogue adds one text notice and no dimming (D-3). Maintenance windows have no row: the contract carries no field (D-9).
- **Live band** (D06 D-4, D-7, §4.2, §7, §11.2).
  - It consumes `ticker.{symbol}` through the app ticker store and holds the topic 30 s after close.
  - Until E08-T08's server producer exists (D06 H-7) it uses the `GET /instruments/{symbol}/ticker` bootstrap. At 5 s that goes stale and stays stale, and it never claims live.
  - A single CMP-239 marker sits in the band header. Thresholds are T1 5 s and T2 15 s (D-4).
  - CMP-126 funding countdown: one fixed-width `hh:mm:ss`, polite at 5 min and 1 min, suppressed when not trading. When the time passes with no fresh ticker it reads "Settlement time passed — waiting for an update", never negative and never a frozen 00:00:00.
  - States: awaiting the first tick, live unavailable (`subscription_limit`), exchange feed down, reconnecting and disconnected.
- **CandleViewer band** (D06 D-10, D-11, §4.3, §8, §11.3).
  - It reads and never subscribes.
  - **Coverage and gaps rows** for the last 90 days come from `GET /market/data-coverage` once per open, with `generated_at` as the as-of.
  - The recording-state rows, first-recorded time and the Owner-only disk, retention and pin rows are E16-S02's; this story renders the slot.
  - For Manager and Viewer, the SCR-140 link is replaced by "Recording is set up by the owner." and "Record this symbol…" is the T2 sentence form, `rbac.owner_only`.
- **States** (D06 §6).
  - Not trading is one deck for PreLaunch, Delivering, Closed and unknown values: "BTCUSDT is not trading on Bybit." (D-5).
  - Catalogue loading runs the 2, 4, 8, 16, 30 s ladder to a 60 s failure.
  - Contract load failed is CMP-027 `role="alert"` once, with Retry.
  - The 404 reads "…isn't in Bybit's instrument list as CandleViewer last read it." with Retry after 60 s.
  - 403 is T4. Coverage failed, tiers unavailable and the clock alarm each stay in their own band.
  - **Rules changed while open** (D-13): changed rows carry "Changed · was 0.01", the band says when, and there is one polite announcement. Nothing swaps silently.
- **Actions:** Open in new chart, and Open DOM ladder only for Trading symbols, read-only for a Viewer. Both open a new panel and never retarget the focused one. There is no order button and no new hotkey (D-15).
- **CMP-125 SymbolInfoPopover** per D06 §9, and the CMP-036 and CMP-046 contract changes A-2 to A-5.
- **Analytics** `symbol.info_viewed`, `symbol.info_load_failed {dependency}`, `symbol.info_rules_changed`, `symbol.info_value_malformed` (`14` SCR-103).
- **Test ids** per D06 §17.3 (`scr103-drawer`, `scr103-band-*`, `scr103-row-<field>`, …) and the forced states listed there.
- **Storybook** for CMP-036, 046, 125, 126 (D06 §17.1 defers these stories to this build).
- **Open owner questions** in D06 stay at their defaults; where a contract field is absent the row reads "not available yet" (D06 §4).

## Out of scope
- Recording-state rows, owner internals (disk, retention, pin) and the "Record this symbol…" action: E16-S02, with the SCR-140 link (E16-S01).
- The contract change requests, to be filed as separate interface-first Tasks (C-6.1): CR-1 (`max_mkt_order_qty` and price bands), CR-4 (risk-limit tiers served), CR-6 (maintenance window), CR-8 (`recording_started_at`), CR-9 (`PendingOpen` mapping), CR-13 (coverage for non-Trading symbols). CR-11 (24 h high and low) is E08-T08's.
- Blocking order entry for a symbol whose rules are not loaded (CR-10, E29 and E08-S02). The drawer says only "CandleViewer can't check BTCUSDT orders against these rules until they load." (D06 §6).
- Pop-out multi-monitor polish beyond one-drawer-per-window (D-16), maintenance windows, and external links (none in the contract).
- The ticker producer (D06 H-7), which is E08-T08.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Contract rules match the API and read as exchange-enforced
  Given the recorded instrument fixture for BTCUSDT
  When the drawer opens
  Then tick size, quantity step, min and max quantity, minimum order value, max leverage and funding interval equal GET /instruments/BTCUSDT
  And each rule shows its sentence and an example computed by the shared rule source
  And the band opens with the sentence that the rules are enforced by the exchange

Scenario: Rules that change while open are marked, never swapped silently
  Given the drawer shows BTCUSDT at revision 7
  When the symbol is re-read and revision 8 carries a different tick size
  Then the changed row shows "Changed · was 0.01" and the band says when
  And one polite announcement follows

Scenario: Stale live data is marked in the live band only
  Given the ticker is 6 seconds old
  Then one freshness marker appears in the live band header and the contract band is neither dimmed nor marked
  And the funding countdown never shows a negative or frozen 00:00:00 value
  And the stale state is announced once

Scenario: A failed contract load is stated, with Retry (failure case)
  Given GET /instruments/BTCUSDT fails with a network error
  Then "Couldn't load BTCUSDT's contract rules." is announced once with role="alert"
  And the order line reads "CandleViewer can't check BTCUSDT orders against these rules until they load."
  And Retry keeps focus on the button and a coverage failure stays inside its own band

Scenario: A Viewer reads the drawer by keyboard
  Given a Viewer session and no pointer use
  Then coverage is shown, "Recording is set up by the owner." replaces the SCR-140 link, and no Record control is in the Tab order
  And Esc closes the drawer and focus returns to the opener
  And axe reports zero serious or critical violations in both themes
```

## Technical notes / design
Estimate 5, as E16-S01 (5: a data-heavy screen). There is a single request, a formatter with sentences, and about 25 rows of states in D06 §6. It is less than E08-S08 because there is no grid or subscription controller. The number-formatting rule (D06 §5, CR-2) and the contract change requests are risks to the schedule, not to the size. The shared formatter is the TypeScript port of E08-S02's rule source, tested against `packages/fixtures/golden/policy/corpus.json`.

## Test plan
Unit: positional decimal formatter across the policy corpus, rules-changed diff, countdown edge cases on a fake clock. Component (RTL): band order and headings, every reachable D06 §6 state, the RBAC variants, focus trap and return. E2E: drawer open from SCR-102 and SCR-100 with recorded fixtures. axe in both themes. Forced states from D06 §17.3 that are not reachable today are listed as waiting on their owner.

## Security notes
Read-only. The Owner-only rows are server-gated; Manager and Viewer get the T2 sentence (`rbac.owner_only`), never a hidden control (E09-D09 A-6). No order action exists in the drawer.

## Accessibility notes
Modal drawer with focus trap and return to the opener; each band is a `section` with an `h3`; one `role="alert"` on contract failure; one polite announcement for stale and rules-changed; the countdown announces only at 5 min and 1 min. axe zero serious or critical in both themes; a screen-reader pass recorded.

## Performance notes
Paints from the warm client index within 100 ms; one contract request and one coverage request per open; the ticker topic is shared through the app store with a 30 s grace.

## Observability
`symbol.info_viewed`, `symbol.info_load_failed {dependency}`, `symbol.info_rules_changed`, `symbol.info_value_malformed` (`14` SCR-103).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario automated against the recorded fixtures; the reachable D06 §17.3 forced states tested, the others listed as waiting on their owner.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80%; axe-core zero serious or critical in both themes; a screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] The formatting rule tested across `packages/fixtures/golden/policy/corpus.json`; Storybook states for the new components; copy matches D06 exactly.

- [ ] Feature flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue with the required approvals.

E17 and E16 are named here and not in the twin's `blocked_by` because the roadmap §11.1 edges run E08 → E16 and E08 → E17; until E16-T08 lands the coverage rows show the D06 §4.3 "not available yet" state. title: Build the SCR-104 scanner panel: live criteria, result cap, estimated flags
body:
## Context
Implements the UI of **US-MKT-001** and **US-MKT-005** for the scanner, and the SCR-104 half of US-DET-001. The risk is a screener that implies precision it does not have (#176 Context). The panel mixes exchange-reported metrics with heuristic estimates (tape-speed z-score, regime) that must carry CMP-227 EstimatedBadge, and it must keep the advice boundary: it shows conditions, never recommendations (#176 Technical notes, R9). It builds the domain components it first needs (E05-S03's deferral), including CMP-024 (the sparkline, which E08-D07 D33 moved here from SCR-100).

**Not Ready until E08-D08 (#176) is Done** (design-ahead DoR, `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1). No D08 spec exists yet, so every item below comes from `14` SCR-104 and the E08-D08 ticket text. **Final copy, layout and states must be taken from the D08 spec once it merges, and this story is re-checked against it before Ready.**

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Scanner pane** in `apps/web/src/features/scanner/` (`14` SCR-104 "Type", "Components").
  - Filter bar (CMP-055) over the criteria 24 h change, volume, funding rate, OI delta, tape-speed z-score, spread and volatility. Regime is estimated (`14` SCR-104 checklist; #176).
  - Estimated criteria carry CMP-227 in the option list itself, plus a one-line derivation note on selection (#176 AC 1).
  - The result table is CMP-049, sortable, with CMP-056 column picker, CMP-011 chips and CMP-024 sparklines. Sparklines are static per refresh and have a numeric neighbour, so trend is never colour-only (#176 accessibility notes).
  - The table caption states the active filter set in plain language, and the result count is announced on change (`14` SCR-104 "A11y"). Filter values render as text only.
- **Data** (`14` SCR-104 "Data", `22` `/scanner`, served by E08-T09).
  - `GET /scanner?filters=&sort=&limit=` polled at ≤0.2 Hz (5 s cadence).
  - **Never evaluate criteria client-side across the universe** (`14` SCR-104 "Performance", #176).
  - The panel is virtualised at the 200-row cap.
  - Per-row `coverage: "live_only"` is explained ("scanning is limited to live metrics for symbols we are not recording").
- **States** (`14` SCR-104 "States", #176 ACs).
  - Capped at 200 with a note that says how to narrow it, and a statement that sorting applies to the capped set.
  - Filter error "Minimum must be less than maximum", inline and naming the filter. The previous results are retained, never cleared to an ambiguous empty state.
  - **No matches and scan failed have separate wording.**
  - A scan whose ticker or OI inputs are stale is marked as computed from possibly stale inputs, using the E08-D04 data-confidence vocabulary, and is not presented as authoritative.
- **Saved presets** are user-scoped and store criteria, never results (#176), through E08-T09's presets endpoint. Behaviour for a preset naming a removed criterion is D08's to specify.
- **Result actions:** open chart (target symbol through the same port as E08-S08), add to watchlist (single and "send matches to watchlist" through `PUT /watchlists`, respecting the 200-symbol list cap, D07 D25), and create alert as an entry point only.
- **Analytics** `scanner.filter_changed`, `scanner.preset_saved`, `scanner.result_opened`, `scanner.alert_created_from_result`, plus an event separating cap-reached from zero-results (`14` SCR-104; #176 Observability).
- Storybook for the filter bar, table and estimated badge states.

## Out of scope
- The scan engine, the query language and the `/scanner` and presets server implementation (E08-T09), and the detector outputs (E25 and the DET epics).
- Alert creation (entry point only), and the order-flow detector algorithms.
- Any account-scoped column (positions, PnL). It needs a separate RBAC review (#176 Security notes). Cross-user preset visibility is forbidden.
- A chart or watchlist surface of its own (E08-S08), and a client-side universe scan under any condition.
- Anything D08 has not signed off. Add no filter, preset UI or layout of our own.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Estimated criteria are flagged before use
  Given the filter bar lists tape-speed z-score and regime
  When the criteria list is opened
  Then both options carry the estimated badge in the option list and the badge has text, not only an icon
  And selecting one shows a one-line explanation of how it is derived

Scenario: The result cap is explained, not silent
  Given more than 200 instruments match
  Then exactly 200 rows are shown with a note that the set is capped and how to narrow it
  And the note states that sorting applies to the capped set
  And the note is linked to the table with aria-describedby

Scenario: An invalid range keeps the previous results (failure case)
  Given a result set is showing
  When the user sets a minimum greater than the maximum
  Then an inline error names the offending filter and the rule "Minimum must be less than maximum"
  And the previous result set stays on screen

Scenario: Stale inputs and a failed scan are not shown as a clean result
  Given the ticker feed is stale when a scan returns
  Then the results are marked as computed from possibly stale inputs and are not presented as authoritative
  Given a scan returns zero rows and another scan errors
  Then each has its own state and wording and neither reuses the other's text

Scenario: The panel is operable and announced without colour or pointer
  Given keyboard-only use and a screen reader attached
  Then every filter is a labelled control and the table caption states the active filters in plain language
  And the result count is announced once per change
  And each sparkline has an adjacent numeric value
  And axe reports zero serious or critical violations in both themes
```

## Technical notes / design
Estimate 5, as E16-S01 and E20-S01 (5). The table and filter bar reuse E08-S08's patterns and the server does the scanning, so it is smaller than E08-S08. The unknowns (presets, estimated criteria wording) sit with D08. Polling is a plain timer with the 5 s cadence; results flow through one store, never per-row state.

## Test plan
Unit: filter validation, caption text from the filter set, poll cadence on a fake clock. Component (RTL): estimated badge in the option list, cap note with `aria-describedby`, no-match versus scan-failed wording, retained results on a validation error. E2E: QA plan case E08-TC-C05 (SCR-104 under reconnect) with recorded fixtures. A 200-row render measured. axe in both themes.

## Security notes
No account-scoped columns; presets are user-scoped and server-enforced (E08-T09), with no cross-user visibility. Filter values are rendered as text only. The advice boundary (R9) holds: the panel states conditions, never recommendations.

## Accessibility notes
Every filter is a labelled control; the caption states the active filters; the result count is announced once per change; sparklines have a numeric neighbour; the estimated badge carries text. axe zero serious or critical in both themes; keyboard-only path and a screen-reader pass recorded.

## Performance notes
Poll ≤0.2 Hz; virtualised at the 200-row cap; no client-side universe evaluation.

## Observability
`scanner.filter_changed`, `scanner.preset_saved`, `scanner.result_opened`, `scanner.alert_created_from_result`, and the cap-reached versus zero-results event (`14` SCR-104).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario automated against recorded fixtures; QA sign-off recorded.
- [ ] Coverage ≥80%; axe-core zero serious or critical in both themes; keyboard-only path and a screen-reader pass recorded.
- [ ] No criteria evaluated client-side; the poll stays at or below 0.2 Hz; a 200-row render measured.
- [ ] Storybook states for new components; copy matches the signed-off D08 text.
- [ ] Docs: `14` SCR-104 updated where the build diverged.
- [ ] Feature flag state recorded; PR merged via the merge queue with the required approvals.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: **E08-D08 (#176, OPEN; this story is Ready only when it is Done)**, E08-D07 (#175), E08-D04 (#125), E08-S01 (#182), E08-S03 (#284), E08-S08 (#4702, the `PUT /watchlists` path for "send matches"), E08-T09 (#4708, the `/scanner` server and presets endpoint), E05-S02 (#265), E05-S03 (#266), E10-S01 (#304). Also consumes E17-T04 (#413, web WS client, Done), named here and not in the twin's `blocked_by` because the roadmap §11.1 edge runs E08 → E17. Blocks E08-Q05 (#282).

Planned for Sprint 07 (2026-11-06 → 11-12). The backlog twin carries `Backlog` because Sprint 07 is over its 45-point holiday capacity in `validate.py`.

title: Recorded Bybit fixture corpus and the demo connectivity smoke-test suite
body:
## Context
Adapter rule 5 (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14.2) is binding: *every adapter ships a contract-test suite run against recorded fixtures, plus an opt-in live smoke test (`pytest -m exchange_smoke`)*. Without a shared corpus, each E08 ticket invents its own ad hoc payloads, integration tests cannot be reproduced, and **R6 Feed rot** - the exchange changing a payload under us - is detected only in production. This Task builds the corpus, the capture tooling that keeps it refreshable, and the demo smoke suite that proves real connectivity.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `packages/fixtures/bybit/` corpus with a documented manifest per fixture (symbol, window, capture date, exchange host, stream, notable event): a clean multi-hour window for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT and one mid-cap symbol; a window containing a **sequence gap**; a window containing a **reconnect**; a window with a **ticker delta-only burst**; a **page-boundary** kline set; error responses for `10018`, `10002` and 5xx; an `instruments-info` payload including a delisted symbol and a changed tick size.
- Capture tool `tools/capture_fixture.py`: connects to the public stream, records raw frames with timestamps, **redacts** anything matching the secret patterns, and emits the manifest. Re-capturable so the corpus can be refreshed when Bybit changes payloads.
- Fixture replay harness shared by all E08 integration tests (deterministic timing, configurable speed) so every ticket asserts against the same inputs.
- `pytest -m exchange_smoke` suite, **opt-in and demo-only**: instrument catalogue fetch, server-time offset, public WS subscribe/receive for each stream, one kline page, clean shutdown. Guarded so it can never run against live and can never run in the default CI job.
- A **payload-drift check**: a scheduled job replays the corpus schema expectations against a freshly captured sample and fails loudly when a field appears, disappears or changes type - the early-warning system for R6.

## Out of scope
- Recording for the product's own replay feature - **E16**/**E23** (different retention, different storage).
- Load-generation fixtures for k6/WS fan-out - **E17**.
- Private/authenticated fixtures - **E29** (no credentials are ever involved here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E08 integration test uses the shared corpus
  Given the E08 test suite
  When it runs offline with no network access
  Then every integration test passes using only packages/fixtures/bybit

Scenario: Fixtures are provably secret-free
  Given the corpus and its manifests
  When the repository secret-scanner runs
  Then no API key, signature, account id or header value is present, and the check is a required CI gate

Scenario: Smoke suite is opt-in and demo-only
  Given the default CI job
  Then no exchange_smoke test executes
  And an attempt to run the smoke suite with a live-environment configuration fails fast with an explicit error

Scenario: Payload drift is detected
  Given Bybit adds, removes or retypes a field in a captured stream
  When the scheduled drift check runs against a fresh sample
  Then it fails with a diff naming the stream and the field, and an issue is raised automatically

Scenario: Replay is deterministic
  Given the same fixture is replayed twice
  Then the produced domain-event sequence is byte-identical, so downstream property tests are reproducible
```

## Technical notes / design
Fixtures are stored as newline-delimited JSON of raw frames plus the manifest, compressed; they are versioned with the capture date in the path so a refresh is additive and an old test can pin an old corpus. The replay harness drives the same `Normalizer` entry point the socket uses, so a test exercises production code rather than a parallel path. The drift check compares against generated schema expectations rather than a golden file, so harmless value changes do not create noise.

## Test plan

title: Ingestion observability, 24h soak harness and doc/ADR reconciliation for R0 exit
body:
## Context
R0 cannot be declared complete on assertions. `docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §5 requires a **24 h ingestion soak on at least three symbols with memory flat within +/-5%** and the architecture docs reconciled with what actually shipped. This Task closes E08: it consolidates the metrics each child emitted into one coherent dashboard and alert set, builds the soak and burst harness that produces the R0 evidence, and reconciles `20-architecture.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md` and the ADRs with the implemented behaviour.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Metric consolidation**: a single `ingestion/metrics.py` registry module owning the names emitted across `E08-T02`/`T03`/`T04`/`S03`/`S04`/`S05`/`S06`/`S07`, with consistent labels (`env`, `exchange`, `symbol`, `stream`) and a test asserting no duplicate or orphaned metric names.
- **Grafana dashboard** "Ingestion" as code (E04 provisioning): connection states, per-stream event rates, ingest lag, queue depth and full-counts, book state/resyncs, staleness by topic, rate-limit headroom, clock drift.
- **Alert rules**: topic staleness beyond threshold, book resync rate above baseline, unrecovered trade gap, clock drift warning/critical, rate-limit headroom exhausted, queue-full on a never-drop class.
- **Soak harness** `bench/ingestion_soak.py`: runs >=24 h against demo on >=3 symbols, sampling RSS, event-loop lag, CPU, queue depths and per-stream latency percentiles; emits a signed-off report artifact.
- **Burst injector**: replays the fixture corpus at 5x for 60 s to prove the never-drop guarantee and measure recovery.
- **Doc/ADR reconciliation**: update `20-architecture.md` §3.1/§3.2/§4 thresholds, `24-internal-schemas.md` §2/§14 mappings, the ADR index; amend ADR-0016 with the soak's real numbers; update `32-risk-register.md` for R3/R6/R7 with measured evidence.
- **Runbook** `docs/ops/ingestion.md`: what each alert means and the first three actions for each.

## Out of scope
- Client-facing WS metrics and load profiles - **E17**.
- Recorder disk-budget measurement - **E16** (this Task hands it the observed bytes/day).
- Epic-level QA regression and the STRIDE model - chunk B tickets.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Soak produces the R0 evidence
  Given the soak runs for 24 hours on three symbols against demo
  Then resident memory is flat within +/-5% end to end
  And ingest->bus p95 <=20 ms, book apply p95 <=2 ms, and the report artifact records all three

Scenario: Burst proves the never-drop guarantee
  Given the corpus is replayed at 5x for 60 seconds
  Then no trade event is lost, queue-full counters reflect applied backpressure
  And steady state is restored within the documented recovery window after the burst ends

Scenario: Every alert has a runbook entry
  Given the merged alert rules
  When they are cross-checked against docs/ops/ingestion.md
  Then every alert has an entry and no entry describes an alert that does not exist

Scenario: Metric drift fails the build
  Given a child module emits a metric name not declared in the registry module
  Then the metrics consistency test fails, naming the offending metric

Scenario: Soak regression is visible
  Given a soak whose memory grows beyond 5%
  Then the harness fails explicitly with the growth curve attached rather than reporting a pass with a caveat
```

## Technical notes / design
The registry module is declaration-first: metrics are declared once with their labels and help text, and modules import them, which is what makes the consistency test possible. The soak harness samples out-of-process (Prometheus scrape + `psutil`) so it does not perturb what it measures, and writes a machine-readable report so the R0 gate reads numbers rather than prose.

## Test plan
Unit: registry consistency, label cardinality guard (symbol cardinality is bounded to the recorded set to prevent a metrics explosion). Integration: dashboard/alert provisioning applies cleanly in the E04 stack. Perf: the soak and burst runs themselves are the deliverable evidence; a short 30-minute variant runs in CI nightly as a regression canary.

## Security notes
Metrics and dashboards must not leak secrets or account identifiers: labels are restricted to the declared set, and a test asserts no label value can carry free-form user input. Dashboard access follows RBAC - Viewer-role users must not reach admin-only panels exposing exchange hosts or key identifiers.

## Accessibility notes
Dashboards and alert text follow `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` where they surface inside the web app's health screens: every status is text plus icon, never colour alone, and alert messages are written as complete sentences an operator can read aloud.

## Performance notes
Observability overhead must stay under 2% CPU at the target event rate; label cardinality is bounded (symbols x streams) and asserted so the metrics backend cost stays predictable - this is a direct R3 Real-time cost control.

## Observability
This Task *is* the observability deliverable: one registry, one dashboard, one alert set, one runbook, plus a meta-alert that fires if the ingestion job stops reporting metrics at all (a silent-death detector for R6 Feed rot).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] 24 h soak report and 5x burst report attached to the ticket and referenced from the R0 exit checklist.
- [ ] Dashboard and alerts merged as code; every alert has a runbook entry.
- [ ] `20-architecture.md`, `24-internal-schemas.md`, `27-adrs/` and `32-risk-register.md` reconciled with shipped behaviour and measured numbers.
- [ ] Metrics consistency and cardinality tests green as required checks.
- [ ] Coverage >=85% on the touched packages; QA sign-off on the soak evidence.

title: /watchlists persistence: migration, routes, RBAC, audit key and version
body:
## Context
SCR-100 and SCR-101 (E08-S08) persist watchlists through `/watchlists`, which exists only in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and the generated models: there is no table in `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` (only the `watchlist` pane kind), no router, and no audit key (`docs/design/E08/E08-D07.md` §12 C-4, C-5, C-7). The design also needs a version or conflict field so a stale write is surfaced rather than silently overwriting (C-1), and a rule for duplicate names (C-3). This Task is the server side; **contract first** (C-6.1): the `22` and `21` edits land in their own small PR before the router.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Contract PR first** (C-6.1, interface-first):
  - `22-api-openapi.yaml`: add `version` (integer, server-assigned) to `Watchlist`; `PUT /watchlists/{watchlistId}` takes `If-Match` (or a `version` in the body, one of the two, decided in the contract PR) and answers `409` (or `412`) with the current version on a mismatch (D07 C-1); `POST` and `PUT` answer `409 watchlist_name_taken` for a duplicate name per user, case-insensitive (D07 C-3, D07 §4.3 "unique per user"); add the `422` responses for over 200 symbols and unknown symbols.
  - `21-database-schema.md`: a `watchlists` table (`id uuid`, `user_id`, `name` 1–80, `symbols text[]` ≤200 in order, `columns text[]`, `version int`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, unique `(user_id, lower(name))`), with its data classification (C-5.9: no credentials or PII beyond the owning user id).
  - `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5: the audit actions `watchlist.created`, `watchlist.updated`, `watchlist.deleted` (D07 C-7), recorded with object kind `watchlist` and the list id; their state carries the name, symbol count and version, never the full list. The audit-vocabulary owner reviews the addition.
  - Regenerate `packages/protocol` and the Python models (`make gen`), never by hand.
- **Migration** (one Alembic revision, additive and reversible, C-5.1/C-5.2): the `watchlists` table and its index.
- **Router** `services/api/candleviewer/api/` for `GET /watchlists`, `POST /watchlists`, `PUT /watchlists/{watchlistId}`, `DELETE /watchlists/{watchlistId}`:
  - RBAC from the contract's `x-rbac`: `workspaces:read` / `workspaces:write`, `scope: self`. A user reads and writes only their own lists; another user's id answers `404`, never `403` (no existence oracle).
  - CSRF on every write, as the existing `/workspaces` routes.
  - Validation with pydantic v2 (`extra="forbid"`): name 1–80, at most 200 symbols, every symbol a known USDT linear perpetual from the instrument catalogue (E08-S01), no duplicates within a list.
  - `PUT` replaces the list and bumps `version` atomically; a version mismatch answers the conflict response with the current version.
  - Each write is audited ahead (C-2.9) with the actions above.
- **Tests**: unit and integration per the Test plan, including the forbidden-role and cross-user (IDOR) cases.

## Out of scope
- The SCR-100 / SCR-101 UI (E08-S08) and the scanner's "send matches to watchlist" (E08-S11).
- A default list and list positions (D07 C-3 leaves them open; not in this contract).
- Pane settings `watchlist_id` and `watchlist_sort` (E15, D07 C-6).
- Sharing a list between users.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A user's lists round-trip with a version
  Given an Owner session
  When the user creates "Majors" with BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT
  Then GET /watchlists returns "Majors" with both symbols in order and version 1
  And PUT /watchlists/{id} with version 1 and a new order answers 200 with version 2

Scenario: A stale write is refused, never applied silently
  Given "Majors" is at version 2
  When a PUT carries version 1
  Then the server answers the conflict response with the current version 2
  And the stored list is unchanged

Scenario: Lists are private to their owner (IDOR)
  Given a Manager session and a list owned by another user
  When the Manager sends GET, PUT or DELETE for that list id
  Then each answers 404 and nothing is changed or revealed

Scenario: Invalid lists are rejected
  Given a create with 201 symbols, an unknown symbol, or a name that already exists for this user in any letter case
  Then each answers its documented 4xx with a problem body naming the field
  And no row is written

Scenario: Every write is audited ahead
  When a list is created, replaced and deleted
  Then watchlist.created, watchlist.updated and watchlist.deleted records exist with the actor, the list id and the version
  And no record carries the full symbol list
```

## Technical notes / design
Estimate 5, against E15-T01 (workspaces migration plus REST API) and E08-T02 (5). Follow the `/workspaces` router, its models and its CSRF dependency as the neighbouring pattern (`api/workspaces.py`, `api/workspaces_models.py`). The version bump and the replace run in one transaction with a row lock; the conflict check is a `WHERE version = :expected` update so two writers cannot both win. One migration in this PR (C-5.3); coordinate the single head with any other in-flight migration.

## Test plan
Unit: pydantic models (limits, duplicates, unknown symbols), version arithmetic. Integration (`@pytest.mark.integration`, real Postgres): CRUD round trip, concurrent PUTs (exactly one wins), IDOR and forbidden-role cases, audit records written ahead, migration upgrade → downgrade → upgrade. Contract: provider tests generated from `22`, Schemathesis on `/watchlists`.

## Security notes
`scope: self` is enforced server-side on every route; cross-user ids answer 404. CSRF on writes. Input validated with `extra="forbid"`; parameterised SQL only. Audit records are append-only and carry no full list. No secrets or credentials are involved.

## Accessibility notes
None directly (backend). The problem bodies name the offending field so E08-S08 can render an inline, programmatically associated error.

## Performance notes
Lists are small (≤200 symbols); `GET /watchlists` p95 ≤ 50 ms on the reference stack with 50 lists per user. No N+1: one query per request.

## Observability
`http_requests_total{route="/watchlists…"}` from the shared middleware; a `watchlist_write_conflicts_total` counter; structured logs with `correlation_id` and the list id, never the symbol list.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Contract PR (`22`, `21`, `24` §15.5) merged before the router; generated code fresh.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario automated; IDOR and forbidden-role cases present.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% line / ≥75% branch on the touched modules; migration round trip recorded.
- [ ] Docs: `21-database-schema.md` `watchlists` and `24` §15.5 reconciled with the build.
- [ ] PRs merged via the merge queue with the required approvals.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: E08-S01 (#182, instrument catalogue for symbol validation), E08-D07 (#175, Done, contract items C-1, C-3, C-4, C-7). Blocks E08-S08 (#4702) and, through it, E08-S11 (#4705).

Planned for Sprint 06 (2026-10-30 → 11-05). The backlog twin carries `Backlog` because Sprint 06 is at its 90-point capacity in `validate.py`.

## Branch
`feat/e08-watchlists-api`

## References
`docs/design/E08/E08-D07.md` §12 (C-1, C-3, C-4, C-5, C-7); `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/watchlists`, `Watchlist`, `WatchlistInput`; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-101 "Analytics/audit"; US-MKT-003.

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/design/E08/E08-D07.md` §12 contract items C-1, C-3, C-4, C-5, C-7, and §4.3–§4.4 (validation rules)
2. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/watchlists`, `Watchlist`, `WatchlistInput`; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` (the `layouts` and `workspaces` tables as the pattern)
3. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5 (audit vocabulary, the `indicator_preset.*` precedent)
4. `services/api/candleviewer/api/workspaces.py` and `workspaces_models.py` (neighbouring router pattern)
5. `.claude/rules/60-database-migrations.md`, `.claude/rules/50-security.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` (contract PR)
- `packages/protocol/` and `services/api/candleviewer/api/_generated/` (regenerated only)
- `services/api/candleviewer/migrations/versions/` (one new revision)
- `services/api/candleviewer/api/` (watchlists router and models), `services/api/candleviewer/audit/` (action registration)
- `services/api/tests/` mirrored unit and integration tests

**Interfaces you must not break**
- the existing `/watchlists` operation ids and `WatchlistInput` fields (additive change only)
- the audit vocabulary's closed-set rule (§15.5: an action needs a code change plus a test)
- the single Alembic head

**Commands** (`AGENTS.md` §4, from `services/api/`)
- `ruff check . && ruff format --check . && mypy --strict .`
- `pytest -m "not integration" --cov=. --cov-fail-under=85`
- `pytest -m integration`
- `alembic upgrade head && alembic downgrade -1 && alembic upgrade head`
- from the repo root after a contract edit: `make gen` then `python tools/ci/check_gen_freshness.py`

**Branch & PR**

- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>` (implementation PR; the contract PR uses `Refs #<issue>`)
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/backend
- Labels: type/task, area/ingestion, priority/p1

**Done means**

- Do not build any UI, a default list, list positions or sharing.

title: Server side of the ticker WS topic, bulk ticker snapshot and 24 h high/low
body:
## Context
The client-facing `ticker` WS topic (`ticker.{symbol}` and the batched `ticker` with `symbols` ≤40, `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1, payload §14.8 `TickerUpdate`) has no server producer. E08-S03 (#284) built the ingestion side (one upstream subscription per symbol, delta merge, bus topic `{env}.md.ticker.{symbol}`) and scoped out "Client-facing WS topic and framing (E17)"; E17-S02 (#378) built the topic registry and subscriptions, but no module supplies `ticker` snapshots or deltas. `docs/design/E08/E08-D06.md` H-7 records it: `ticker` "is not even in `ws_wiring.py`'s `PENDING_ADAPTERS`", so a `ticker.{symbol}` subscription stays `snapshot_pending` (`23` §7.7), and nothing calls `GatewayHub.instrument_revision` on `InstrumentUpdatedEvent`. Until this lands, SCR-100 rows read "Not live" and the SCR-103 live band never leaves its REST bootstrap.

This Task is the **producer side**: E08-S03's bus topic → the E17-S02 topic registry. E17-S02 (#378) is the **consumer side** (subscriptions, per-topic authorisation, fan-out) and is not changed here beyond registering the adapter. It also owns two gaps the designs route to the ticker owner: the bulk snapshot `GET /market/tickers?symbols=` (`docs/design/E08/E08-D07.md` §12 C-11; E08-D05 Q3, A-D05-14) and 24 h high and low (E08-D06 CR-11). **Contract first** (C-6.1) for every `22`, `23` and `24` change.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Contract PR first** (C-6.1):
  - `22-api-openapi.yaml`: `GET /market/tickers?symbols=` (up to 200 symbols, a list's cap), `x-rbac` `marketdata:read`, answered from a server-side cache of one Bybit linear `GET /v5/market/tickers` call refreshed at most every 5 s and shared by every client; each item carries the `Ticker` fields and its `ts`; unknown symbols are reported, not dropped silently (D07 C-11).
  - `23-ws-protocol.md` §14.8: state the semantics of the per-item `stale` flag (D07 C-2: set when the symbol's merged state is older than the 5 s staleness threshold E08-S03 uses, cleared on the next fresh push) and confirm `high_24h` / `low_24h` population; record the `ticker` family in §7.7 "As built".
  - `24-internal-schemas.md` §2 `TickerEvent`: add `high_24h` and `low_24h` (from Bybit `highPrice24h` / `lowPrice24h`) if absent (D06 CR-11).
  - Regenerate `packages/protocol` and the Python models (`make gen`).
- **Ticker adapter** for the gateway (`services/api/candleviewer/ws_wiring.py` and the owning ingestion module):
  - A snapshot source for `ticker.{symbol}` and the batched `ticker` from E08-S03's per-symbol merged state; a delta publisher from the `{env}.md.ticker.{symbol}` bus topic, throttled and coalesced per `23` §8 (250 ms default).
  - Upstream demand flows through the existing `IngestionUpstreamSink` lease (one upstream subscription per symbol, 30 s grace, E08-S03).
  - The 40-symbol per-connection cap and the rebuild budget stay the registry's (E17-S02); this adapter adds no bypass.
  - A first subscription to a symbol whose merged state is still warming stays `snapshot_pending` until the state is complete, never a half-populated `snap`.
- **`instrument_revision` caller:** on `InstrumentUpdatedEvent` call `GatewayHub.instrument_revision(symbol)` so subscribed clients get the `23` §7.4 re-snapshot (D06 H-7, D-13).
- **Bulk snapshot route** `GET /market/tickers` in `services/api/candleviewer/api/` with the shared 5 s cache and a bounded single-flight refresh.
- **Normaliser** maps `highPrice24h` / `lowPrice24h` into `TickerEvent` and the REST `Ticker` (`api/ticker.py` today returns `high_24h: None`).
- Recorded, redacted fixtures for the bulk `tickers` REST answer if none exist (`packages/fixtures/bybit/`, in a capture's dated directory with a `manifest.json` entry, C-13.5).

## Out of scope
- The SCR-100, SCR-103 and SCR-102 UIs (E08-S08, E08-S10, E08-S09).
- Subscription management, authorisation, the 40-symbol cap and the rebuild limit (E17-S02 #378; `23` §16.2), and the `recorder` topic (E16-T08, D07 C-10).
- `/market/open-interest` (E24-T01, #665) and open-interest history.
- Any change to the upstream Bybit subscription planner (E08-T04) or the delta-merge rules (E08-S03).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A ticker subscription is snapped and then streamed
  Given the recorded BTCUSDT ticker fixture is replaying through ingestion
  When a client subscribes to ticker.BTCUSDT
  Then it receives one snap with a complete TickerUpdate and then d frames no more often than every 250 ms
  And every frame validates against the 23 §14.8 schema

Scenario: The batched topic shares one upstream subscription per symbol
  Given two connections subscribe to ticker with symbols BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT
  Then ingestion holds exactly one upstream subscription per symbol
  And closing both connections releases each after the 30-second grace

Scenario: A warming symbol is never snapped half-populated
  Given the first message after an upstream subscribe is a partial delta
  Then the subscription stays snapshot_pending until the merged state is complete

Scenario: An instrument revision re-snapshots subscribers
  Given a client holds ticker.SOLUSDT
  When InstrumentUpdatedEvent arrives for SOLUSDT
  Then the client receives a server-initiated resync snap per 23 §7.4

Scenario: The bulk snapshot is shared and bounded (failure case)
  Given 20 clients request GET /market/tickers for the same 120 symbols within 5 seconds
  Then exactly one upstream tickers call is made and each answer carries every item with its ts
  Given the upstream call fails
  Then the route answers 503 with a problem body and serves no value older than its documented bound as current
```

## Technical notes / design
Estimate 5, against E08-S03 (3: the ingestion side) and E08-T02 (5): an adapter on an existing registry plus one cached REST route and a normaliser field. The adapter is plain asyncio code on the hot path; no statechart (C-2.20). Coalescing is `CONFLATE_LATEST` like the bus topic. The bulk cache uses single-flight with an `asyncio.timeout` on the upstream call and a bounded refresh queue (C-2.18).

## Test plan
Unit: snapshot assembly from merged state, warming hold, `stale` flag computation on a fake clock, normaliser high/low mapping, bulk cache single-flight and expiry. Integration: fixture replay through ingestion → bus → gateway → a test WS client, asserting frame schemas, throttle, refcounted upstream leases and the revision re-snapshot. Contract: provider test for `/market/tickers`; WS frames validated against `23` §14.8. Chaos: upstream drop mid-stream (C-13.6 scenarios 2 and 4).

## Security notes
Public market data only; topic names are built from catalogue-validated symbols (E08-S01). The bulk route caps `symbols` at 200 and validates each; the cache is shared and holds no per-user data. No Bybit host is called from tests (recorded fixtures only, C-13.5). Rate budget: the bulk refresh is one public call per 5 s at most and draws from the adapter's public budget, never the order reserve (C-12.7).

## Accessibility notes
None directly (backend). The `stale` flag gives SCR-100 and SCR-103 the text-bearing stale state US-MKT-003 requires.

## Performance notes
Bus → WS frame p95 ≤ 20 ms added latency; one upstream subscription per symbol; bulk route p95 ≤ 50 ms from cache; a stalled consumer holds at most one coalesced ticker per topic.

## Observability
`cv_ws_snapshot_build_seconds{topic="ticker"}`, `cv_ws_stale_topics_in_use`, `ticker_bulk_cache_refresh_total{outcome}`, `ticker_bulk_cache_age_seconds`; logs carry `connection_id`, never a payload.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Contract PR (`22`, `23` §14.8 and §7.7, `24` §2) merged before the adapter; generated code fresh.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario automated against recorded fixtures.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% line / ≥75% branch on the touched modules; perf numbers recorded against the budgets.

`blocked_by`: E08-S03 (#284, ingestion side, Done), E08-S01 (#182). Consumer side: E17-S02 (#378, Done), named here and not in the twin's `blocked_by` because the roadmap §11.1 edge runs E08 → E17. Blocks E08-S08 (#4702); serves E08-S10 (#4704) and E08-S09's 24 h values (D05 Q3).
