title: GET /scanner server and saved scanner presets endpoint
body:
## Context
SCR-104 (E08-S11) polls `GET /scanner`, which exists only in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and the generated models: there is no router in `services/api`, and the `ScannerFilter` schema its `filters` parameter names is not defined. The E08-D08 ticket (#176) also requires user-scoped **saved presets** that store criteria, never results, and `22` has no preset endpoint. This Task is the server side of both; **contract first** (C-6.1) for every `22` and `21` change.

`GET /market/open-interest` was checked for an owner: E24-T01 (#665, "Open-interest ingest, REST backfill and /market/open-interest endpoint") owns it, so it is not in this Task's scope.

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Contract PR first** (C-6.1):
  - `22-api-openapi.yaml`: define `ScannerFilter` (a closed set of criteria, each with optional `min` / `max` as decimal strings; at least the criteria `14` SCR-104 lists: 24 h change, volume, funding rate, OI delta, tape-speed z-score, spread, volatility, regime; criteria that are estimates are marked `estimated: true` in a criteria descriptor so the UI can badge them); a `GET /scanner/criteria` descriptor list (id, label, unit, `estimated`, `needs_recording`) if the contract PR finds the client needs it; `422` for `min > max` naming the criterion; add `turnover_24h`, `funding_rate` and `spread_bps` to `ScannerRow` only where `14` SCR-104 needs them.
  - Presets: `GET /scanner/presets`, `POST /scanner/presets`, `PUT /scanner/presets/{presetId}`, `DELETE /scanner/presets/{presetId}`, `x-rbac` `marketdata:read` for read and the user's own write permission for writes, `scope: self`, CSRF on writes; a preset stores `name` (1–80) and a `ScannerFilter`, never results.
  - `21-database-schema.md`: a `scanner_presets` table (`id`, `user_id`, `name`, `filter jsonb`, `version`, timestamps, unique `(user_id, lower(name))`), with its data classification (C-5.9).
  - `24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5: audit actions `scanner_preset.created`, `.updated`, `.deleted` (following the `indicator_preset.*` precedent: state carries a content hash, not the filter). The audit-vocabulary owner reviews the addition.
  - Regenerate `packages/protocol` and the Python models (`make gen`).
- **Migration** (one Alembic revision, additive and reversible): `scanner_presets`.
- **Scanner service and router** (`services/api/candleviewer/api/` plus a market-data service module):
  - Evaluates the filter set over the most recent values in `tickers` and `orderflow_metrics` (`22` `/scanner` description), server-side only.
  - Symbols without active recording get `coverage: "live_only"`; criteria that need recorded history are skipped for them, never evaluated as zero.
  - Sort per the contract enum; `limit` capped at 200; `DataMeta` carries the input freshness so the client can mark a scan computed from possibly stale inputs (E08-D04 vocabulary).
  - Results are cached per normalised filter for a short window (≤ 5 s) so 0.2 Hz polling from several panes costs one evaluation.
- **Presets router**: CRUD with server-side validation of the stored filter against the current criteria set; a preset naming a criterion the server no longer knows is returned with that criterion flagged, never silently dropped (final UI behaviour is E08-D08's).

## Out of scope
- The SCR-104 UI (E08-S11) and its copy, layout and preset UI (E08-D08, #176).
- The detector algorithms behind tape speed, regime and liquidation intensity (E25 and the DET epics); this Task reads their latest stored values.
- `/market/open-interest` (E24-T01, #665).
- Alert creation from a result (entry point only, in the UI).
- Account-scoped columns (positions, PnL) and cross-user preset visibility.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A filter set is evaluated server-side and capped
  Given recorded ticker and order-flow fixtures for 300 symbols
  When GET /scanner is called with a 24 h change filter that 250 symbols match and limit 200
  Then exactly 200 rows are returned in the requested sort order
  And meta states that the set was capped

Scenario: Symbols without recording are explained, not zeroed
  Given a filter on tape speed and a symbol that is not recorded
  Then its row carries coverage "live_only" and the tape-speed criterion is skipped for it
  And it is not ranked as if its tape speed were zero

Scenario: An invalid range is refused (failure case)
  When a filter sets min greater than max for funding rate
  Then the server answers 422 with a problem body naming the funding-rate criterion

Scenario: Presets are private and store criteria only
  Given an Owner saves preset "Momentum" with a filter set
  Then GET /scanner/presets for that user returns the name and the filter and no results
  And a Manager requesting the same preset id answers 404
  And the create is audited ahead as scanner_preset.created

Scenario: Polling from several panes costs one evaluation
  Given three panes poll the same filter every 5 seconds
  Then the scanner evaluates that filter at most once per cache window
```

## Technical notes / design
Estimate 5, against E08-T02 (5) and E15-T01 (migration plus REST). The evaluation is a read over the latest `tickers` and `orderflow_metrics` rows per symbol; push the filter into the query where the store allows, and run any remaining CPU work off the event loop (`asyncio.to_thread`) if it exceeds ~1 ms (C-2.18). The filter is parsed with pydantic v2 (`extra="forbid"`) before any query is built; parameterised SQL only. One migration in this PR (C-5.3); coordinate the single head with E08-T07's.

## Test plan
Unit: `ScannerFilter` parsing and validation, `live_only` skipping, sort and cap, cache keying on the normalised filter. Integration (`@pytest.mark.integration`): evaluation over seeded QuestDB/Postgres data from recorded fixtures; presets CRUD with IDOR and forbidden-role cases; audit ahead; migration upgrade → downgrade → upgrade. Contract: provider tests and Schemathesis on `/scanner` and `/scanner/presets`. Perf: a 500-symbol evaluation timed.

## Security notes
The `filters` query is bounded (4000 chars) and parsed into a closed schema before use; no raw SQL fragments from input. Presets are `scope: self`, cross-user ids answer 404, CSRF on writes, audit written ahead with a content hash rather than the filter. No account-scoped data is exposed. The advice boundary (R9) holds: the API returns conditions, never recommendations.

## Accessibility notes
None directly (backend). The `422` problem body names the criterion so E08-S11 can show an inline error tied to that filter.

## Performance notes
`GET /scanner` p95 ≤ 200 ms for 500 symbols from cache-cold, ≤ 20 ms from cache; one evaluation per filter per cache window regardless of the number of polling panes.

## Observability
`scanner_evaluations_total{outcome}`, `scanner_evaluation_seconds`, `scanner_cache_hits_total`, `scanner_capped_total`; preset writes counted by the shared HTTP middleware; logs carry `correlation_id`, never the filter values.

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Contract PR (`22`, `21`, `24` §15.5) merged before the implementation; generated code fresh.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario automated against recorded fixtures; IDOR and forbidden-role cases present.
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% line / ≥75% branch on the touched modules; migration round trip recorded; perf numbers recorded.
- [ ] Docs: `21` `scanner_presets` and `24` §15.5 reconciled with the build.
- [ ] PRs merged via the merge queue with the required approvals.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: E08-S01 (#182, symbol catalogue), E08-S03 (#284, `tickers`). The criteria list follows `14` SCR-104 and #176's ticket text; if E08-D08 (#176) changes a criterion before this Task starts, follow D08. Blocks E08-S11 (#4705).

Planned for Sprint 07 (2026-11-06 → 11-12). The backlog twin carries `Backlog` because Sprint 07 is over its 45-point holiday capacity in `validate.py`.

## Branch
`feat/e08-scanner-api`

## References
`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/scanner`, `ScannerRow`, `DataMeta`; `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.11 `orderflow_metrics`, `tickers`; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-104; issue #176 (E08-D08); US-MKT-001, US-MKT-005, US-DET-001.

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/scanner`, `ScannerRow`, `DataMeta`
2. `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-104 and issue #176 (E08-D08) for the criteria and presets rules
3. `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md` §4.11 `orderflow_metrics` and `tickers`; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5
4. `services/api/candleviewer/api/workspaces.py` (user-scoped CRUD pattern) and `api/market.py` (market-data route pattern)
5. `.claude/rules/60-database-migrations.md`, `.claude/rules/50-security.md`

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, `docs/plan/21-database-schema.md`, `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` (contract PR)
- `packages/protocol/` and `services/api/candleviewer/api/_generated/` (regenerated only)
- `services/api/candleviewer/migrations/versions/` (one new revision)
- `services/api/candleviewer/api/` (scanner and presets routers), the market-data service module, `services/api/candleviewer/audit/`

**Interfaces you must not break**

**Commands** (`AGENTS.md` §4, from `services/api/`)

title: Serve POST /instruments/refresh: RBAC, job and poll, rate limits, failure path
body:
## Context
SCR-102 (E08-S09) calls `POST /instruments/refresh` from its Owner-only **Refresh from Bybit** action, in Load failed and in the stale footer; its design then polls the job the route returns through `GET /admin/jobs/{job_id}` and reads a `failed` or `cancelled` job as **Refresh failed** (`docs/design/E08/E08-D05.md` §6.2; `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-102). The operation, `refreshInstruments`, is declared in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` and generated into the models, and E08-S01's scope listed it, but no ticket served it: E08-S01 (#182) and its slice E08-S01-2 (#1607) are closed, #1607 delivered the two read routes only, and no open ticket owns the route (PR #5067, E08-S09 PR C2, records the gap). It sits in `services/api/tests/unit/architecture/composition_allowlist.json` under `openapi_pending` and in `services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml` as `not_mounted` (gap G1 of `docs/qa/e08-signoff.md`). Until it is served, SCR-102 answers every refresh with its fallback copy ("Couldn't request a refresh just now."), and the job poll and Refresh failed that wait on the route cannot be built or tested end to end. This Task serves the route over the scheduler and the job store that already exist (`InstrumentsRefreshScheduler`, `AdminJobStore`) and the poll that already exists (`getJob`). It invents no contract: what 22 left open is RULED under Technical notes (Q1 to Q6), and the route PR's first commit puts what those rulings change into 22 and 24 (C-6.1).

## Scope / Deliverables
- **Contract first, in the route PR's first commit** (C-6.1): `22` states what Q1, Q2 and Q4 rule (the join, the route's own limit, the `Job` envelope for `instrument_refresh`) and `24` §15.5 gains the `instruments.refresh.requested` and `instruments.refresh.completed` actions (Q3). `packages/protocol` and the Python models are regenerated (`make gen`), never by hand. The route follows in the PR's later commits.
- **Route** `POST /instruments/refresh` (`refreshInstruments`) in `services/api/candleviewer/api/instruments.py`, beside `GET /instruments` and `GET /instruments/{symbol}`:
  - RBAC from the contract's `x-rbac`: `instruments:write`, `scope: none`. Only the Owner holds it (`auth/rbac_seed.json`: a dangerous permission, granted through the Owner's `*`); the RBAC matrix row is Owner allow, Manager and Viewer `403`, unauthenticated `401`. Server-side and fail-closed like the neighbouring reads: no principal resolver wired answers `501`, no session `401`, a missing permission `403`. The UI's T2 hint (the session's permission claims) is never the control.
  - CSRF on the write (22's `CsrfToken`, SR-041): a missing or mismatched token answers `403 csrf_token_invalid`.
  - `Idempotency-Key` optional (`x-idempotency: optional`): the same key replays the original `202` for 24 h with `Idempotency-Replayed: true` (22 "Idempotency").
  - Answers `202` with `{job_id, scheduled_at}` and never awaits the fetch; `503` when the catalogue scheduler is not wired or has stopped (the reads' 503 causes); `403` and `429` as the contract lists them.
  - A request while a refresh is queued or running joins it (Q1): `202` with the running job's `job_id`, no second job, no second venue spend and no `409`. The route checks for a running refresh first, then its own 60 s limit (Q2), and only then starts a job.
  - Step-up is E09's dangerous-permission policy, applied by citation (Q5): this ticket adds no step-up class and no exemption of its own.
  - **Audit, write-ahead (C-2.9; Q3):** `instruments.refresh.requested` with the actor, role, env and job id, written before the route answers `202` (and, for a new job, before the job exists), as `api/recorder_admin.py` writes the recorder routes' records. A request whose record cannot be written answers `503 audit_unavailable` and starts nothing (`24` §15.5). The job's terminal state is audited as a second action, `instruments.refresh.completed` with `status: succeeded | failed`, written by the job's `on_done` hook (Q3); `AdminJobStore` audits nothing itself, and each recorder route audits its own the same way.
- **Job and poll**: the request submits a job of kind `instrument_refresh` to the admin job store (`AdminJobStore.submit`, `api/recorder_admin.py`), so the existing `GET /admin/jobs/{jobId}` (`getJob`, `admin:read`, `api/admin_jobs.py`) polls it with no new route. The job runs one catalogue refresh through the scheduler (`refresh_now`, which serialises with the periodic and on-demand refreshes under the scheduler's lock) and ends `succeeded`; `failed` when the scheduler's retries are spent (`InstrumentRefreshError`: the previous catalogue keeps serving, marked stale); or `cancelled` when the process is stopping and the job store cancels its tasks. The job's `result` and `error` are the job store's existing `getJob` envelope (Q4), with no new field and no new shape.
- **The failure path SCR-102 reads** (E08-D05 §6.2): a `failed` or `cancelled` job is what SCR-102 renders as Refresh failed ("results kept"), so a failed refresh must leave the previous catalogue served with `meta.stale_since` set (E08-S01's "Refresh fails" scenario) and count `instruments_refresh_total{result="error"}`; a job lost to a restart answers `404` with rule `job_unknown` (22 `getJob`: jobs live in the API process's memory, ADR-0004), which SCR-102 treats as the end of the poll.
- **Rate limits against the venue budget** (C-12.7): the job's fetches ride the `MARKET_DATA` class (`24` §1.3, the S-RL note: the stop, cancel and SL reserve is untouched), so a refresh never draws on that reserve. The request is refused `429` with `code: exchange_rate_limited`, `Retry-After` and `retry_after_seconds` when the venue budget has no token for it, and with `code: rate_limited` over the per-user bucket (22 "Rate limiting" and `RateLimited`; the two copy lines of E08-D05 §6.2). **The route's own limit (Q2):** one accepted refresh per environment per 60 s; a request beyond it answers `429` with `Retry-After`, creates no job and spends nothing. A request that joins a running refresh (Q1) starts no refresh, so this limit neither refuses nor counts it.
- **Mount and baselines**: wire the route and the job store in `services/api/candleviewer/app.py`; remove `POST /instruments/refresh` from `openapi_pending` in `composition_allowlist.json` and lower `PENDING_BASELINE` and `FROZEN_BASELINE` in `services/api/tests/unit/architecture/test_composition_guard.py` by one each (the guard fails on a stale entry, and the frozen baseline may only shrink); flip the RBAC matrix row to `state: executed`.
- **Tests**: unit, integration and contract per the Test plan, including the forbidden-role, unauthenticated, CSRF, replay, join, 60 s limit and audit cases.

## Out of scope
- The SCR-102 client half: the job poll (2, 4, 8, 16 and 30 s, one in flight), the Refresh failed footer and the 60 s bound of the 202 notice (E08-D05 §6.2; `14` SCR-102 "As built"). #451 (E12-S11) owns it, consumer side (Q6).
- The scheduler's periodic 12 h refresh, the unknown-symbol on-demand refresh and its 60 s cooldown, and the risk-limit tiers (S-RL, #913): unchanged.
- A new job store, a new poll route or a new `Job` kind: `instrument_refresh` and `getJob` are in 22.
- A refresh of one symbol, and any non-`linear` category.
- Deciding the route's step-up: E09's dangerous-permission policy applies by citation (Q5).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: The Owner's refresh is scheduled and polled to its end
  Given an Owner session and a loaded catalogue
  When the Owner sends POST /instruments/refresh
  Then the route answers 202 with a job_id and a scheduled_at, without waiting for the fetch
  And GET /admin/jobs/{job_id} reports kind instrument_refresh, queued or running, then succeeded
  And GET /instruments then reports a reset cache_age_s and no stale_since

Scenario: A failed refresh ends as a failed job and keeps the old catalogue
  Given the exchange fails every attempt of the refresh
  When the job ends
  Then its status is failed with a stable error code and no message text, in the job store's existing envelope
  And GET /instruments still serves the previous catalogue with stale_since set
  And instruments_refresh_total{result="error"} has incremented

Scenario: Only the Owner may refresh
  Given a Manager session, a Viewer session and an unauthenticated caller
  When each sends POST /instruments/refresh
  Then the answers are 403, 403 and 401, no job exists and no exchange call was made

Scenario: Rate limits answer with the contract's 429 codes
  Given the venue budget has no token for the MARKET_DATA class
  When the Owner sends POST /instruments/refresh
  Then the answer is 429 with code exchange_rate_limited, Retry-After and retry_after_seconds, and no job is created
  And a request over the per-user bucket answers 429 with code rate_limited

Scenario: A repeated request replays as the contract says
  Given the Owner sent POST /instruments/refresh with an Idempotency-Key
  When the same key is sent again within 24 hours
  Then the original 202 is replayed with Idempotency-Replayed true and no second job exists

Scenario: A write without a matching CSRF token is refused
  Given an Owner session
  When the Owner sends POST /instruments/refresh with a missing or mismatched CSRF token
  Then the route answers 403 csrf_token_invalid, no job exists and no exchange call was made

Scenario: A request while a refresh runs joins it
  Given a refresh job is queued or running
  When the Owner sends POST /instruments/refresh
  Then the route answers 202 with the running job's job_id, and never 409
  And no second job exists and no second venue call was made

Scenario: A second refresh inside 60 seconds is refused with Retry-After
  Given a refresh was accepted for this environment less than 60 seconds ago and has ended
  When the Owner sends POST /instruments/refresh
  Then the route answers 429 with Retry-After, creates no job and makes no venue call
  And once 60 seconds have passed since that accepted refresh, a new request is accepted

Scenario: The request is audited ahead of the answer
  Given an Owner session
  When the Owner sends POST /instruments/refresh
  Then instruments.refresh.requested is written with the actor, role, env and job id before the route answers 202 and before the job exists
  And a request whose record cannot be written answers 503 audit_unavailable and starts no job
  And when the job ends, instruments.refresh.completed is written with its status, succeeded or failed
```

## Technical notes / design
Estimate 3, against E08-T07 (5: a migration, four routes and a contract PR) and E08-S01 (3: the catalogue and its two reads): one route over a scheduler, a job store and a poll that already exist, with no migration, plus the composition wiring, the failure path and the matrix and guard edits. Follow `api/instruments.py` (the reads' fail-closed RBAC and 503 rule) and `api/recorder_admin.py` (a `202` over `AdminJobStore`, its idempotency record, its write-ahead audit and its single flight, `JobConflict`, which this route turns into Q1's join where the recorder routes answer `409`) as the neighbouring patterns. The router reaches the scheduler through a narrow `Protocol`, as `CatalogueReader` does, so it never imports the exchange adapter. The problem bodies carry a stable `code`, and a `429` carries `retry_after_seconds`, which SCR-102 reads by `code` and status only.

**Open questions, all RULED** (the orchestrator, 2026-10-30). Each entry gives the decision and closes the alternative, and the route PR does not reopen it. Its first commit puts what Q1, Q2 and Q4 rule into `22` and Q3's action into `24` §15.5 (C-6.1):
1. **Q1, a request while a refresh is queued or running. RULED: `202` with the running job's `job_id`.** The caller joins the job: no second job, no second venue spend, no `409`. Closed: `409 job_running`, which the recorder job routes answer (`/admin/recorder/import`, `/admin/recorder/compact`).
2. **Q2, the route's own limit. RULED: one accepted refresh per environment per 60 s, `429` with `Retry-After` beyond it.** The venue spend goes through the adapter's per-UID budget class (`MARKET_DATA`, `24` §1.3), never the stop, cancel and SL reserve (C-12.7). A join (Q1) starts no refresh, so it is checked first and is not counted. Closed: no cooldown beyond the single flight, the per-user bucket and the `MARKET_DATA` headroom check.
3. **Q3, audit. RULED: yes, write-ahead (C-2.9): `instruments.refresh.requested` with the actor, role, env and job id.** The action is contract-first in `24` §15.5 and is added to `AUDIT_ACTIONS` (`services/api/candleviewer/audit/actions.py`, a C-10.2 path) with its test in the same PR. **The job's terminal state is audited too (RULED 2026-10-30, 18:53Z): a second action, `instruments.refresh.completed` with `status: succeeded | failed`,** written by the job's `on_done` hook, as each recorder route writes its own; an admin action that spends venue budget leaves its outcome in the audit. Both actions are contract-first in `24` §15.5. Closed: no terminal record.
4. **Q4, the job's outcome. RULED: the job store's existing `getJob` envelope, contract first in `22` (the route PR's first commit); no new shape.** `result` and `error` are the envelope's own fields, filled as the store fills them for every kind: `error` is a stable code, never a message (a typed refusal's `code`, else the exception's class name). Closed: any new `result` or `error` shape for `instrument_refresh`.
5. **Q5, step-up. RULED: E09's dangerous-permission policy applies by citation (the SR row for `instruments:write`).** `instruments:write` is seeded `dangerous` (`21` §10.1), and the dangerous-route registry sweep (`services/api/tests/unit/api/test_dangerous_route_registry.py`, SR-E42-01) holds every mounted operation that needs a dangerous permission to that policy. This ticket cites the policy and never decides it: it adds no step-up class and no exemption. **No SR row covers `instruments:write` yet, so the implementing PR's own first commit (docs, contract first, as #5048 did) adds the `04` §7.2.2 `refreshInstruments` row and `instruments:write` to SR-025's list, and the sweep passes at mount (RULED 2026-10-30, 18:53Z; named under Interfaces).** Closed: the proposal of no step-up.
6. **Q6, the SCR-102 client half. RULED: #451 (E12-S11) owns the job poll and the Refresh failed footer, consumer side.** #4703's hand-off note (`issuecomment-6523861575`) already routes the opener binding to #451, and the poll and the footer go to the same note. This Task is the server half. Closed: E08-S09's remaining PR (#4703 is closed) and a new ticket.

The three readings the build made are confirmed (RULED 2026-10-30, 18:53Z): a join is checked before the 60 s limit and is not counted by it; the audit record precedes every `202`, a join included; and a failed audit write answers `503 audit_unavailable` and starts nothing, in `24` §15.5's form.

## Test plan
Unit: the route with fakes (a scheduler, a job store, a principal resolver, an audit writer, a clock): the `202` body, `401`, `403`, `501` and `503`, the CSRF refusal, the `429` mapping with its `Retry-After`, the idempotent replay, the join (a running job answers its own `job_id` and nothing is submitted), the 60 s limit (refused with `Retry-After` inside the window, accepted after it, a join never counted) and the audit record (written before the answer and before the job exists, with the actor, role, env and job id; a failed write answers `503 audit_unavailable` and starts nothing; the job's end writes `instruments.refresh.completed` with `succeeded` or `failed`); a scheduler fake that never returns proves the handler does not await the fetch. The job: `succeeded`, `failed` (the scheduler raises `InstrumentRefreshError`: the store's stable error code, no message) and `cancelled` (the store stops). Integration (`@pytest.mark.integration`; recorded fixtures only, no network, C-13.5): the route through the real scheduler on the recorded `instruments_before.json` and `instruments_after.json` (under `packages/fixtures/bybit/2026-10-05/rest/`: a baseline catalogue, then a delisting and a tick-size change); the failure path with the recorded `error_503.json` leaves the previous catalogue served with `stale_since` set. E08-TC-A05, A08 and A10 of `qa/plans/e08-market-data-test-plan.md` drive the scheduler directly today (`docs/qa/e08-signoff.md` G1) and are re-pointed at the route; A10 expects a synchronous Problem response on a venue 5xx, which the contract's `202` job does not give, so it is re-written to the job's `failed` and the unchanged catalogue. Contract: the provider test generated from `22` and Schemathesis on `/instruments/refresh`; the RBAC matrix row runs as `executed`; the composition guard passes with the entry removed and both baselines lowered; the dangerous-route registry sweep passes with the route recorded as E09's policy gives it (Q5); the audit vocabulary test holds `instruments.refresh.requested` and `instruments.refresh.completed` in `AUDIT_ACTIONS` and in `24` §15.5.

## Security notes
`instruments:write` is a dangerous permission held by the Owner only, enforced server-side on the route (C-12.4); the UI's T2 hint is not a control. The route is state-changing: CSRF on the write (SR-041) and the idempotency record. A refresh spends the shared venue budget, so it rides `MARKET_DATA` only, never the stop, cancel and SL reserve (C-12.7), and a flood answers `429` before any fetch. An upstream error body is never echoed in an answer, a job `error` or a log (E08-TC-A10). The request is audited write-ahead (C-2.9, Q3): `instruments.refresh.requested` names the actor, role, env and job id, the job's end is audited as `instruments.refresh.completed` with its status, and both actions live in `services/api/candleviewer/audit/`, a C-10.2 path. Step-up is E09's dangerous-permission policy, applied by citation and never decided here (Q5). No key, secret or account is involved: the fetch is a public market-data read. The `security` label records the dangerous permission, the budget guard, the audit action, the step-up citation and the RBAC matrix row, whose file is CODEOWNED by `@CandleViewer/security`.

## Accessibility notes
None directly (backend). A failed refresh is what SCR-102 announces once through its polite region (E08-D05 §9.2); the problem bodies carry a stable `code` and, on `429`, `retry_after_seconds`, so the client can say "try again in N s" in text.

## Performance notes
The route only schedules: p95 ≤ 50 ms on the reference stack, as E08-S01's reads, with no upstream call on the request path. One refresh runs at a time (the scheduler's lock, and Q1's join). Record the duration of a refresh on the reference stack against SCR-102's poll span, 60 s in all (2 + 4 + 8 + 16 + 30 s): a refresh that outlasts it ends the notice with no verdict (E08-D05 §6.2). The scheduler's own bounds apply (three attempts; the tier fetches' 15 s budget, `RISK_LIMITS_REFRESH_BUDGET_S`).

## Observability
`http_requests_total{route="/instruments/refresh"}` from the shared middleware (`403` and `429` are visible by status); `instruments_refresh_total{result}` and `instruments_cache_age_seconds` (E08-S01, existing) must move on a refresh; structured logs with `correlation_id` and the `job_id`, never an upstream body. The audit records `instruments.refresh.requested`, written ahead, and `instruments.refresh.completed` with the job's status (Q3).

## Definition of Done
- [ ] Q1 to Q6 are RULED on this ticket; the route PR's first commit carries the contract change (`22` for Q1, Q2 and Q4; `24` §15.5 for Q3's action), generated code fresh.
- [ ] Every Gherkin scenario automated; the forbidden-role, unauthenticated, CSRF, replay, join, 60 s limit and audit cases present.
- [ ] The route served: the allow-list entry removed, both baselines lowered, the RBAC matrix row `executed`.
- [ ] `instruments.refresh.requested` and `instruments.refresh.completed` registered in `AUDIT_ACTIONS` with their tests, and the route recorded under E09's dangerous-permission policy by citation (Q5).
- [ ] Coverage ≥85% line / ≥75% branch on the touched modules; E08-TC-A05, A08 and A10 re-pointed at the route.
- [ ] Docs: `14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-102 "As built" no longer says the route is a stub waiting on E08-S01, and `docs/qa/e08-signoff.md` G1 names this ticket as closing it.
- [ ] PR merged via the merge queue with the required approvals.

## Dependencies
`blocked_by`: none open. What it builds on is merged and closed: E08-S01 (#182) and its slice E08-S01-2 (#1607), the scheduler and the two reads; E16-T05 (#489) and E42-T05 (#966), the admin job store and `getJob`; E08-D05 (#126), the answers' copy and the poll. Q1 to Q6 are RULED on this ticket, and Q5 cites E09's dangerous-permission policy. Blocks the SCR-102 client's job poll and Refresh failed, which #451 (E12-S11) owns on the consumer side (Q6) and which wait on this route.

Planned for Sprint 07 (2026-11-06 → 11-12), train R1 (Charting alpha), with its 3 points accepted as an overage: ledger addendum A row A48 (#2701, `issuecomment-6527955222`) records it in `ACCEPTED_OVERAGE` in `validate.py` as Sprint 07 +3 (+5 in all) and train R1 +3 (+5 in all), funded from the R5 defect and polish reserve as A24 was, and no other ticket moves. The reason is the consumer: E08-S09 (#4703) has merged the quick-switcher that spends the shared on-demand refresh, and a consumer never ships without its route. `validate.py` finds no room for 3 points in Sprints 06 to 20 (Sprint 19 would take train R3 over its 540-point cap), and Sprint 21, the first sprint with room, is four months after the consumer.

## Branch
`feat/e08-instruments-refresh-api`

## References
`docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `refreshInstruments`, `getJob`, `Job`, "Idempotency", "Rate limiting", `RateLimited`, `CsrfToken`; `docs/design/E08/E08-D05.md` §6.2 (Refresh answered, Refresh failed, the 429 copy, the poll), §10 (RBAC), §16 (the route as a dependency); `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-102 "As built"; `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §1.3 (S-RL, the `MARKET_DATA` class), §15.5 (audit vocabulary); `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §4.3; `docs/qa/e08-signoff.md` G1; `qa/plans/e08-market-data-test-plan.md` E08-TC-A05, A08, A10; E08-S01 (#182) and E08-S01-2 (#1607); PR #5067 (E08-S09, PR C2); #451 (E12-S11); `services/api/tests/unit/api/test_dangerous_route_registry.py` (SR-E42-01); US-MKT-001; CONSTITUTION C-2.9, C-6.1, C-12.4, C-12.7.

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `refreshInstruments`, `getJob`, `Job` (kind `instrument_refresh`), "Idempotency", "Rate limiting" and `RateLimited`
2. `docs/design/E08/E08-D05.md` §6.2 (Refresh answered, Refresh failed, the 429 copy and the poll), §10 (RBAC) and §16 (the route as a dependency)

4. `services/api/candleviewer/api/recorder_admin.py` (`AdminJobStore`, `JobConflict`, a `202` over a job, the write-ahead audit) and `services/api/candleviewer/api/admin_jobs.py` (`getJob`)
5. `services/api/tests/unit/architecture/test_composition_guard.py` (`openapi_pending`, the two baselines), `services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml`, `.claude/rules/50-security.md`
6. `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5 and `services/api/candleviewer/audit/actions.py` (`AUDIT_ACTIONS`), and `services/api/tests/unit/api/test_dangerous_route_registry.py` (the step-up sweep, Q5)

**Repo paths to create/modify**
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` (Q1, Q2 and Q4) and `docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §15.5 (Q3's action): the route PR's first commit
- `packages/protocol/` and `services/api/candleviewer/api/_generated/` (regenerated only)

- `services/api/candleviewer/audit/actions.py` (`AUDIT_ACTIONS`) and its test under `services/api/tests/unit/audit/`
- `services/api/candleviewer/api/step_up.py` and `services/api/tests/unit/api/test_dangerous_route_registry.py` (the route's entry, only as E09's policy gives it: Q5)
- `services/api/tests/unit/architecture/composition_allowlist.json`, `services/api/tests/unit/architecture/test_composition_guard.py`, `services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml`

**Interfaces you must not break**

- the `GET /instruments` and `GET /instruments/{symbol}` answers, and the scheduler's `refresh_now`, `ensure_symbol` and `ensure_fresh` behaviour
- the audit vocabulary's closed-set rule (§15.5): `instruments.refresh.requested` and `instruments.refresh.completed` are added with `AUDIT_ACTIONS` and their tests in the same PR, and no existing action changes

**Branch & PR**
- Branch: `feat/e08-instruments-refresh-api` (one PR; its first commit is the contract change, C-6.1)
- PR title: "E08-T10: Serve POST /instruments/refresh: RBAC, job and poll, rate limits, failure path"
- PR description includes: `Closes #<issue>`
- Required reviewers (CODEOWNERS): @CandleViewer/backend, plus @CandleViewer/security for `services/api/tests/contract/rbac/matrix.yaml` and for `services/api/candleviewer/audit/`, and @CandleViewer/architecture for `packages/protocol/` (the contract commit)
- Labels: type/feature, area/ingestion, priority/p1, security

**Done means**
- Q1 to Q6 are RULED on the ticket; the route PR's first commit carries the contract change; generated code fresh.
- Every Gherkin scenario automated, including the forbidden-role, unauthenticated, CSRF, replay, join, 60 s limit and audit cases.
- The route served: the allow-list entry removed, both baselines lowered, the RBAC matrix row `executed`.
- `instruments.refresh.requested` and `instruments.refresh.completed` registered in `AUDIT_ACTIONS` with their tests; the route recorded under E09's dangerous-permission policy by citation.
- Coverage ≥85% line / ≥75% branch; the QA plan rows and the two doc notes updated.

**Do NOT**
- Do not build the SCR-102 job poll or the Refresh failed footer (Q6), or any other UI.
- Do not answer `409` to a request while a refresh runs: it joins the running job (Q1).
- Do not decide the route's step-up here: E09's dangerous-permission policy applies by citation (Q5).
- Do not add a route, a job store or a `Job` field for this: `getJob` and the kind `instrument_refresh` exist.
- Do not await the venue fetch on the request path, or call the exchange adapter from the route.
- Do not draw on the stop, cancel and SL reserve: the refresh rides `MARKET_DATA`.
- Do not echo an upstream body or message in an answer, a job `error` or a log.
- Do not gate the route on the UI's T2 hint, or skip the forbidden-role case.
- Do not hand-edit generated code, or leave the allow-list entry and the baselines as they were.

**If blocked**
- Comment on this ticket's GitHub issue naming the exact blocking condition (missing contract, failing upstream gate, ambiguous acceptance criterion) and the ticket key it depends on. Move the issue's Status to **Blocked**. Do not silently work around a failing gate, widen scope, or guess at an undocumented contract — stop and wait for the blocker to clear.

title: UX research: how traders read staleness, gaps and resync in live data
body:
## Context
E08 (Bybit adapter & ingestion skeleton, modules M3 Exchange adapter interface, M4 Bybit v5 adapter, M5 internal bus, M6/M7 book reconstruction) is the first epic in the programme that produces *conditionally trustworthy* data. `US-MKT-005` requires a "reconnecting" state rather than stale values, `US-MKT-006` requires gapped windows to be marked as gapped after a sequence gap or REST backfill, `US-MKT-007` requires dependent views to show "resyncing" while the L2 book is re-seeded, and `US-MKT-003` requires watchlist cells to grey out with a stale marker "rather than showing frozen values as if live".

Those three requirements describe a single cross-cutting UX primitive that does not exist yet: a **data-confidence vocabulary** (live / stale / reconnecting / resyncing / gapped / backfilling / delisted). Getting the vocabulary wrong is a trading-safety problem, not a cosmetic one — a frozen price that looks live can cause a real order at a wrong price. This research ticket exists so that the hi-fi work in E08-D02..E08-D10 is grounded in evidence rather than designer intuition, and so the design-system contribution in E08-D04 is defined once rather than re-invented per panel.

The audience is small and known (`10-personas.md`: the Owner/principal trader, and account managers), so this is a qualitative study: structured interviews plus a stimulus-based comparison task, not a statistically powered test.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Research plan and discussion guide covering the stories `US-MKT-003`, `US-MKT-005`, `US-MKT-006`, `US-MKT-007`, `US-MKT-008`, `US-MKT-009`.
- 4–6 sessions (Owner + available managers + 2 external perp traders if recruitable) covering: (a) what they currently do when a feed looks frozen on TradingView/Bybit/DeepCharts; (b) recognition test of 3 candidate visual treatments per state; (c) tolerance thresholds — how long a gap must be before it must be visible at all.
- Stimulus set: static comparison boards for the *stale* and *reconnecting* treatments applied to `SCR-100` Watchlist panel, `SCR-053` Tape panel and `SCR-050` DOM ladder + heatmap panel; and for the *gapped window* treatment on the chart price axis region.
- Findings report at `docs/research/findings/E08-data-confidence.md` with: a recommended state vocabulary (names + definitions + precedence order when two states co-occur), recommended time thresholds (when a cell becomes stale, when a banner escalates), and explicit "do not do this" anti-patterns.
- Decision log entries for anything that contradicts the current wording in `14-screens-catalogue.md` (`SCR-100`, `SCR-152`) so those docs are corrected rather than silently diverged from.
- Input handoff to E08-D02 (wireframes) and E08-D04 (design-system contribution) recorded as comments on those tickets.

## Out of scope
- Any pixel-level or hi-fi visual design — that is E08-D03, E08-D05..E08-D10.
- Order-entry or execution safety research (owned by the E2x trading epics); this study covers *market data confidence only*.
- Quantitative usability benchmarking / SUS scoring — the participant pool is too small to be meaningful.
- Mobile or Android contexts (out of scope per owner decision 2026-09-14).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Study executed and reported
  Given the research plan is approved by the CDO
  When at least 4 sessions have been run and transcribed
  Then a findings report exists at docs/research/findings/E08-data-confidence.md
  And it defines every state in the data-confidence vocabulary with a one-line definition and a precedence rule

Scenario: Recommendations are actionable by design and engineering
  Given the findings report is published
  When a designer opens E08-D02 or an engineer opens an E08 ingestion story
  Then each recommended state maps to a named condition the backend can actually emit (e.g. last-message age, sequence gap detected, resync in progress, REST backfill in progress)
  And any recommendation the ingestion layer cannot currently detect is filed as an explicit gap with a linked follow-up

Scenario: Evidence contradicts an existing catalogue statement
  Given participants consistently misread the greyed-out stale treatment described for SCR-100
  When the findings are reviewed
  Then a correction to 14-screens-catalogue.md SCR-100 is raised in the same sprint
  And the superseded wording is recorded in the decision log rather than deleted silently

Scenario: Colour-only signalling is rejected (edge/failure)
  Given a candidate treatment distinguishes live from stale by hue alone
  When it is evaluated against 05-accessibility-standard.md
  Then it is recorded as rejected in the report with the reason
  And a non-colour redundant channel (text, icon, opacity plus label) is recommended in its place

Scenario: Sessions cannot be recruited
  Given fewer than 4 external participants are available
  When the study is executed with Owner plus managers only
  Then the report states the reduced sample explicitly as a validity limitation
  And the CDO records whether the reduced evidence is sufficient for sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Anchor stimuli in real conditions: use recorded Bybit fixtures (the same fixtures E08 integration tests use) so the shown densities and update rates are realistic, not invented.
- Run the comparison task in a neutral tool (static boards or a Figma prototype); do not build throwaway front-end code.
- Cover the co-occurrence matrix explicitly: stale + delisted, reconnecting + gapped, resyncing + backfilling. Precedence must be total (no ambiguous pairs) or the hi-fi work cannot be consistent.
- Capture *thresholds as numbers*, because they become configuration in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` terms and defaults in the client.

## Test plan
- Peer review of the discussion guide by a second researcher for leading questions before session 1.
- Pilot session (not counted in the 4) to validate stimulus legibility and timing.
- Analysis triangulated by two people coding the transcripts independently; disagreements resolved and noted.

- Every candidate treatment must be evaluated against `05-accessibility-standard.md`: redundant encoding beyond colour, contrast of the degraded/stale state against the surface (a greyed cell still needs AA contrast for its text), and an announced equivalent for screen-reader users.

## Performance notes
- Any recommended treatment must be cheap at watchlist/tape/DOM update rates: the report must flag treatments that imply per-cell animation or per-update layout changes, because `SCR-100` coalesces ticker updates to 4 Hz and the tape/DOM run far hotter.
- Thresholds must be expressed so they can be evaluated with a single timestamp comparison per row, not per-pixel work.

title: Wireframes: market-data connection, staleness and resync states
body:
## Context
Before any hi-fi screen work, E08 needs a single low-fidelity structural pass that decides *where* connection and data-confidence information lives across the app: a global banner (`SCR-152` Disconnected / reconnecting state), per-panel treatments, per-row treatments (`SCR-100` Watchlist panel) and per-field treatments (`SCR-103` Symbol info drawer live block). Deciding this once, structurally, prevents each subsequent hi-fi ticket from inventing its own placement and prevents the classic failure where three different indicators contradict each other on one screen.

The ingestion behaviours that must be representable come straight from the adapter design: WS reconnect with exponential backoff and resubscribe (`US-MKT-005`), sequence-gap detection with REST backfill and a gapped window (`US-MKT-006`), book invalidation and re-snapshot (`US-MKT-007`), paged historical backfill with rate-limit backoff (`US-MKT-008`), and clock-offset drift (`US-MKT-009`).

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Wireframe set (low-fi, greyscale, annotated) in Figma covering:
  - `SCR-152` Disconnected / reconnecting — global banner anatomy, attempt/backoff countdown, "Trading is disabled while offline" and "Your exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected" lines, `Retry now` / `Details` actions.
  - `SCR-100` Watchlist panel — stale row/cell treatment, delisted row, subscription-cap state.
  - `SCR-053` Tape panel and `SCR-050` DOM ladder + heatmap panel — per-panel "resyncing" overlay placement (structure only; visual design belongs to the consuming epics).
  - `SCR-103` Symbol info drawer — live block vs static contract-spec block separation, so a stale live field never makes the contract specs look stale.
  - `SCR-147` Admin: exchange connectivity & rate limits — placement of clock-skew indicator and throttled/banned states.
  - `SCR-151` Empty state pattern — the "data not recorded yet" / "backfill in progress" variants.
- A **state placement matrix**: rows = data-confidence states from E08-D01, columns = surfaces, cells = which indicator level (global / panel / row / field) is authoritative, plus the precedence rule when several apply.
- Annotated flow sketches for: disconnect → backoff attempts → reconnect → resubscribe → resync → live; and gap detected → REST backfill → gapped window marked.
- Open-questions list routed to the Architect and the E08 engineering lead.

## Out of scope
- Colour, typography, iconography, motion — E08-D03, E08-D04, E08-D11.
- The DOM/tape/chart panels' own content design (owned by their epics); this ticket only fixes where the confidence layer sits on them.
- Copywriting final strings (drafted here, finalised in E08-D03 with the content reviewer).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every ingestion condition has exactly one authoritative surface
  Given the state placement matrix is complete
  When any data-confidence state is selected
  Then exactly one indicator level is marked authoritative for it on each surface
  And the precedence rule resolves every co-occurring pair without ambiguity

Scenario: Reconnect flow is representable end to end
  Given the reconnect wireflow
  When walked with the E08 engineering lead against the adapter's actual lifecycle (drop, backoff attempt n, resubscribe, snapshot re-seed)
  Then every transition the backend can emit has a wireframe frame
  And any backend transition with no frame is either given one or explicitly marked as not user-visible with a reason

Scenario: A frozen value can never masquerade as live (failure case)
  Given a wireframe for SCR-100 with a symbol whose ticker stream has dropped
  When reviewed
  Then the last value is either visually demoted with an explicit stale label or replaced by a dash with a timestamp of last update
  And no frame shows an unchanged value with unchanged styling

Scenario: Two states at once
  Given a symbol is both delisted and its feed is stale
  When the wireframe is reviewed
  Then delisted wins per the precedence rule and the stale marker is suppressed
  And the frame is annotated with that rule

Scenario: Review sign-off
  Given the wireframes are complete
  When reviewed by CDO, Architect and the accessibility specialist
  Then all blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Use the ASCII anatomies already in `14-screens-catalogue.md` (`SCR-100`, `SCR-152`) as the starting structure rather than inventing new layouts — divergence must be deliberate and noted.
- Keep the global banner non-blocking: it must not reflow panel content on appearance (reserve space or overlay), because reflow during a reconnect storm is both ugly and a performance problem.
- Annotate every state with the backend condition that drives it, named exactly as E08 will expose it (last-message age, gap detected, resync in progress, backfill in progress, clock offset > 500 ms per `US-MKT-009`).
- Model the "grace period" from `US-MKT-005` (30 s unsubscribe grace) so panels do not flicker on rapid open/close.

## Test plan
- Structured walkthrough with the E08 engineering lead against the adapter lifecycle (documented above as an AC).
- Design critique with 2 product designers + design-system representative.
- Accessibility pre-review: check that each state has a text equivalent planned and a sensible focus/announcement story before hi-fi starts.
- Cross-check against `18-traceability-matrix.md` rows for `US-MKT-003`, `US-MKT-005`, `US-MKT-006`, `US-MKT-007` to confirm no referenced screen was missed.

## Security notes
- The `Details` affordance on `SCR-152` must not expose internal endpoints, API keys, account identifiers or raw exchange error payloads to non-owner roles; wireframe annotations must state the RBAC-filtered content (Owner sees diagnostic detail; Manager/Viewer see a plain status).
- No wireframe may show an API key, secret or signed URL, even as placeholder text.

## Accessibility notes
- Each state must be annotated with: the accessible name/description, whether it is announced (`role="status"` vs `role="alert"`), and the rate-limit for announcements on a flapping connection.
- The banner must be reachable and dismissible (where dismissal is allowed) by keyboard, and must not steal focus from an in-progress interaction.
- Stale rows must remain readable: contrast requirements are annotated, not left to the visual pass.

## Performance notes
- Annotate which indicators update at what cadence: watchlist 4 Hz coalesced (per `SCR-100`), banner countdown at 1 Hz max, panel overlays event-driven only.
- Forbid per-row animation in the wireframe annotations for surfaces that can hold 200 symbols (`SCR-100` cap) — the treatment must be a static style change.

## Observability
- Annotate the analytics events each state should emit (`data_confidence.state_entered`, `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}`) so instrumentation is specified before implementation.

## Definition of Done
- Wireframe file and state placement matrix published in Figma and linked from this ticket and from `14-screens-catalogue.md` entries touched.
- Walkthrough with engineering completed and open questions closed or explicitly deferred with owners.
- CDO sign-off comment recorded; Status set to **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done).
- Handoff to E08-D03/D04/D05/D07/D09/D10 noted on those tickets.

title: Hi-fi: SCR-152 disconnected / reconnecting banner and per-panel treatment
body:
## Context
`SCR-152` is the single most safety-relevant surface E08 introduces: it is what the trader sees when the Bybit public WS drops, when the adapter is backing off, when a topic is resubscribing and when the L2 book is being re-seeded. The catalogue already fixes its content (`attempt n, next in n s`, last-data age, "Trading is disabled while offline", "Your exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected", `Retry now` / `Details`), so this ticket turns that into a production-ready hi-fi spec with all states, tokens, and RBAC variants — and defines the per-panel degraded treatment that other epics will reuse verbatim.

This design is consumed by the E08 ingestion stories in Sprint 02–04 and, later, by every live surface, so it must be signed off in Sprint 01.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-152` in light and dark themes, at the supported densities from `16-design-system-brief.md`, covering states: connected (banner absent) · degraded (some topics stale) · reconnecting with attempt/countdown · disconnected beyond threshold · resyncing book · backfilling history · clock-skew warning (`US-MKT-009`, offset > 500 ms) · recovered (transient confirmation).
- RBAC variants: Owner (diagnostic `Details` with adapter state, topic list, last error class incl. rate-limit `10018`) vs Manager/Viewer (plain status, no internals).
- Per-panel degraded treatment spec applied to `SCR-050` (DOM ladder + heatmap), `SCR-053` (Tape), `SCR-100` (Watchlist panel) — overlay vs inline, what stays interactive, what is disabled.
- Final copy for every string, content-reviewed; no placeholder lorem.
- Component usage: `CMP-028` Callout / Banner (new variants if needed, routed through E08-D04), `CMP-023` Progress Bar for backfill, `CMP-019` Icon, `CMP-001` Button, `CMP-021` Link, `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge where a value is derived rather than exchange-reported.
- Redline/spec page: spacing, tokens, motion references (pointing at E08-D11), z-index and stacking relative to modals and the command palette.

## Out of scope
- Order-entry disablement behaviour and its copy in the ticket itself (owned by the trading epics) — this ticket only states that trading is disabled and links.
- Replay-mode banners (`SCR-152` is live-only here; replay states belong to the replay epic).
- Motion timing curves themselves (specified in E08-D11; referenced here).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: All states designed and tokenised
  Given the hi-fi file is complete
  When each of the eight states is inspected
  Then every colour, spacing and type value resolves to a design-system token, not a raw hex or magic number
  And both light and dark themes are present for each state

Scenario: Safety statements are always present when trading is affected
  Given the disconnected or reconnecting state
  When the banner is rendered
  Then it states that trading is disabled and that exchange-side stop-losses are unaffected
  And neither line can be truncated at the narrowest supported viewport

Scenario: Diagnostic detail is role-gated (failure/abuse case)
  Given a Viewer role session in the disconnected state
  When Details is opened
  Then no endpoint, account identifier, API key fragment or raw exchange payload is shown
  And the Owner variant shows the diagnostic content instead

Scenario: Flapping connection does not produce a strobing UI (edge case)
  Given the connection drops and recovers repeatedly within a few seconds
  When the spec is reviewed
  Then the banner defines a minimum visible duration and a debounce before it reappears
  And the announcement policy prevents repeated screen-reader alerts

Scenario: Long outage
  Given the connection has been down beyond the escalation threshold from E08-D01
  Then the banner escalates its severity styling and shows the age of the last data
  And the Retry now action remains available and keyboard reachable

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given review by CDO, accessibility specialist and the E08 engineering lead
  Then all blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- The banner must be implementable as an overlay that does not reflow the workspace (decided in E08-D02); the spec states the reserved region and the behaviour when a modal is open.
- Countdown text is derived from the adapter's backoff schedule — the spec must define rounding (whole seconds) and the wording when the next attempt is imminent (`retrying…`).
- "Last data" age must be defined precisely: age of the newest message across subscribed topics, not per-topic, with the per-topic breakdown in `Details`.
- Rate-limit (`10018`) and exchange 5xx are distinct error classes with distinct copy; both map to the same visual severity but different explanation and recovery hint.
- Provide the degraded-panel spec as a reusable pattern so E12/E16/E17 consume rather than copy.

## Test plan
- Design review + critique; accessibility design review scheduled as part of E08-D12.
- Contrast verification of every state in both themes with a token checker (AA for text, AA non-text for the status iconography).
- Copy review by the content reviewer; truncation test at the narrowest and widest supported viewport widths.
- Walkthrough with QA/SDET to confirm each state is externally observable and therefore testable in Playwright (a stable test id per state is specified).

## Security notes
- Explicit RBAC content split for `Details` (above) — documented in the spec, not implied.
- No raw exchange error bodies surfaced to any role; only mapped error classes from the adapter error taxonomy.
- The banner must never claim trading is safe when the app cannot verify state; copy is reviewed against `R9 Advice boundary` wording rules.

## Accessibility notes
- Banner is `role="status"` when degraded and `role="alert"` when trading is disabled; announcement rate-limited per E08-D01.
- `Retry now` and `Details` are in the focus order immediately after the banner text; focus is not stolen on appearance.
- Per-panel overlays must not trap focus and must expose the panel's state via `aria-describedby` on the panel region.
- All state distinctions carry an icon + text, never colour alone; the stale treatment keeps AA text contrast.

## Performance notes
- Countdown updates at ≤1 Hz; the spec forbids per-frame animation of banner content.
- Per-panel overlays must be a single composited layer with no per-row work, so a 200-row watchlist or a hot tape panel is unaffected.
- The banner must not trigger layout of the chart canvas; annotated in the redlines.

## Observability
- Specify `data_confidence.state_entered {surface, state, duration_ms}` emission points and the `connectivity.reconnect_forced` audited event on `Retry now` (already catalogued on `SCR-147`).
- Specify stable test/analytics identifiers per state for Playwright and for dashboards.

## Definition of Done
- Hi-fi frames, all states, both themes, fully tokenised; redline page complete.
- Copy final and content-reviewed; RBAC variants documented.
- New/changed component variants raised against E08-D04 and accepted by the design-system team.
- `14-screens-catalogue.md` `SCR-152` entry updated where the design diverged from the original description.
- CDO sign-off comment recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done) — at least 2 sprints before the consuming FE story.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E08-D02.
- Feeds E08-D11 (motion), E08-D12 (a11y review), E08-D13 (handoff), E08-D14 (design QA).

## Branch
`design/e08-hifi-scr152-connection`

## References

- `docs/plan/15-component-catalogue.md` `CMP-001`, `CMP-019`, `CMP-021`, `CMP-023`, `CMP-028`, `CMP-227`

## Agent execution brief

**Read first**

title: Design-system contribution: data-confidence tokens, states and badges
body:
## Context
The data-confidence vocabulary defined in E08-D01 and placed in E08-D02 will be consumed by essentially every live surface in the product (watchlist, tape, DOM, heatmap, chart series, CVD, positions). If it is expressed as ad hoc styling inside `SCR-152` and `SCR-100`, every downstream epic will re-implement it slightly differently and the product will be inconsistent exactly where consistency is a safety property. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 also forbids ad hoc one-off components: "any new component has a design-system entry".

This ticket therefore contributes the vocabulary to the design system as tokens + a small set of catalogued components/variants, so E08 engineering and all later epics consume a single source.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- **Tokens** added to `16-design-system-brief.md`: a `data-confidence.*` semantic token set (live, stale, reconnecting, resyncing, gapped, backfilling, delisted) mapping to surface, text, border and icon roles in both themes, with contrast-verified values.
- **Component contributions** to `15-component-catalogue.md`:
  - `CMP-028` Callout / Banner — new `connection` severity variants used by `SCR-152`.
  - `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge — confirm/extend contract so "estimated" and "stale/gapped" never collide visually (they are different claims: derived vs untrustworthy).
  - A new atom/molecule entry for the per-value freshness marker used by `CMP-161` WatchlistRow, `CMP-036` KeyValueRow live fields and tape/DOM cells — proposed as a design-system entry with full contract (tiers, props, a11y, tokens), allocated an ID by the design-system team.
  - `CMP-026` EmptyState — new `variant="backfill-in-progress"` and confirmation of `variant="recording-not-started"` usage for `SCR-151`.
- **States matrix** documented per component: default, hover/focus where interactive, each confidence state, and the disabled/degraded composition.
- Figma library publication of the above, with the components named exactly as catalogued so handoff (E08-D13) is unambiguous.

## Out of scope
- Motion definitions (E08-D11) beyond referencing the token names.
- Screen-level layout (the hi-fi tickets).
- Building the React components — that is engineering work in the consuming stories.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Vocabulary exists exactly once
  Given the contribution is published
  When any E08 hi-fi frame uses a confidence state
  Then it references the published token/component and defines no local style
  And a lint of the Figma file reports zero detached instances for these states

Scenario: Contrast holds in both themes
  Given every data-confidence token pair
  When checked against WCAG 2.2 AA
  Then text-on-surface pairs meet 4.5:1 (or 3:1 for large text) and non-text indicators meet 3:1
  And any pair that fails is corrected before sign-off, not waived

Scenario: Estimated and stale are distinguishable (edge case)
  Given a value that is both heuristically derived and stale
  When rendered
  Then the estimated badge and the freshness marker are both present and visually separable
  And the catalogue documents the composition rule

Scenario: A consumer needs a state we did not define (failure case)
  Given a later epic requires a confidence state not in the set
  When it is raised
  Then the process documented on this ticket requires a design-system change request rather than a local variant
  And the catalogue entry names that process

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given review by the design-system team lead, the accessibility specialist and the CDO
  Then the entries are merged into 15-component-catalogue.md and 16-design-system-brief.md
  And the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Express confidence as a *semantic* token layer over the base palette so theming and future brand changes do not require re-deciding safety semantics.
- The freshness marker must be renderable as a pure CSS class change (no extra DOM node per cell) for hot surfaces; note that constraint in the component contract so engineering implements it that way.
- Delisted is a catalogue fact, not a feed condition — keep it a separate token group with the precedence rule from E08-D01 written into the contract.
- Provide a machine-readable token export (JSON) alongside the doc entries so the web app consumes tokens rather than transcribing them.

## Test plan
- Automated contrast check over the exported token JSON (script run in the design-system pipeline); results attached to the ticket.
- Visual regression baseline captured for each component state in both themes once implemented (baseline images specified here, captured by engineering).
- Review that every E08 hi-fi ticket's frames resolve to these tokens (checked again during E08-D13 handoff and E08-D14 design QA).
- axe-core rules identified for the implemented components (name/role/value for status markers).

## Security notes
- No security-sensitive content in tokens themselves; however the catalogue entries must state that confidence components never render raw exchange error text, only mapped classes, preventing accidental leakage through a generic "reason" prop.
- The `Details`-style props on the banner variant are documented as RBAC-filtered by the caller.

## Accessibility notes
- Each component contract specifies: accessible name pattern, whether the state is exposed via `aria-*` or visually-hidden text, announcement policy, and the non-colour redundancy channel.
- Freshness marker must expose its meaning to screen readers per row without flooding — contract specifies a summarised region announcement rather than per-cell live regions.
- Reduced-motion behaviour for any state transition is part of the contract (defers detail to E08-D11).

## Performance notes
- Contract forbids per-instance animation and additional DOM nodes on hot surfaces; states must be a class toggle.
- Token export is static; no runtime computation of colours.
- Note the 4 Hz coalescing budget from `SCR-100` and the far higher tape/DOM rates as the design constraint the contract is written against.

## Observability
- Catalogue entries specify the analytics hook names (`data_confidence.state_entered`) so instrumentation is consistent across consumers.
- Design-system adoption tracked: a follow-up check during E08-D14 lists any consumer using a local style instead of the token.

## Definition of Done
- `15-component-catalogue.md` and `16-design-system-brief.md` updated and merged; Figma library published and versioned.
- Token JSON export available to the web app.
- Contrast check green; component contracts include a11y and performance clauses.
- Consumers (E08-D03, D05, D07, D08, D09, D10) updated to reference the published components.
- CDO and design-system lead sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done).

title: Hi-fi: SCR-102 symbol search and SCR-041 quick-switcher from the catalogue
body:
## Context
E08 delivers the instruments-info cache (`US-MKT-001`) that every symbol-selection surface reads from. `US-MKT-002` demands type-ahead results in <=50 ms from the local catalogue with full ARIA combobox semantics, and explicit handling of the v1 scope boundary ("v1 supports Bybit USDT linear perpetuals only") and of delisted symbols. Two surfaces consume this: the global modal `SCR-102` Symbol search and the compact in-chart `SCR-041` Symbol/interval quick-switcher.

These are the first surfaces where E08's catalogue freshness (12-hour refresh, on-demand refresh for unknown symbols, delisted status) becomes visible, so the design must show catalogue state, not just results.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-102` (modal, `Ctrl+P`): idle with recents/favourites, typing with matched-substring highlighting, results with metadata (24 h change, volume), per-result actions (open chart, add to watchlist, open ladder), recording indicator, no-results with the scope reminder, catalogue-stale/refreshing state, delisted result treatment.
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-041` (in-chart quick-switcher): symbol field, interval field, keyboard-only path, delisted banner entry point, narrow-width behaviour.
- Components used and specified: `CMP-048` Combobox / AutoComplete, `CMP-160` SymbolSearchInput, `CMP-213` FuzzyList, `CMP-219` SymbolPicker, `CMP-220` IntervalPicker, `CMP-011` Tag / Chip, `CMP-026` EmptyState, `CMP-021` Link.
- Interaction spec: keyboard map (open, navigate, select, per-result action, escape-and-restore-focus), ranking/highlight rules, and the exact behaviour when the catalogue has not loaded yet.
- Copy for the scope reminder, the delisted explanation and the refresh state, content-reviewed.

## Out of scope
- The command palette `SCR-012` itself (hosts search but is owned elsewhere) - only the shared `CMP-213` behaviour is aligned here.
- Watchlist management flows (`SCR-101`, covered in E08-D07).
- Server-side search/scanner design (`SCR-104`, covered in E08-D08).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Keyboard-only operation is fully specified
  Given the interaction spec
  When a keyboard-only path from opening search to switching the focused chart's symbol is traced
  Then every step has a defined key, a visible focus treatment and an announced change
  And Esc closes the modal and restores focus to the previously focused element

Scenario: Scope boundary is explicit on no results
  Given a query matching no USDT linear perpetual
  When the no-results state renders
  Then it states that no USDT perpetual matches the query and that v1 covers linear perps only
  And it offers a next action rather than a bare 'No data'

Scenario: Delisted symbol (edge case)
  Given a symbol whose exchange status is no longer Trading
  When it appears in history, favourites or an existing chart
  Then it is visually marked as delisted with an explanation, is not offered as a new selection, and order entry entry points are absent
  And the frame is annotated with the precedence rule against the stale marker

Scenario: Catalogue not yet loaded (failure case)
  Given the instruments cache is empty or refreshing on first start
  When search is opened
  Then a loading state is shown that does not present an empty result list as 'no matches'
  And a retry path is available if the refresh fails

Scenario: Highlighting does not rely on colour
  Given a fuzzy match with highlighted substrings
  When reviewed against 05-accessibility-standard.md
  Then the highlight uses weight or background plus sufficient contrast, not hue alone

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO, accessibility specialist and the E08 engineering lead have reviewed
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Results come from the local cached catalogue (`GET /api/v1/instruments`, refreshed hourly client-side / <=12 h server-side per `US-MKT-001`); design must make a common-case network round-trip unnecessary - no spinner in the typing path.
- Ranking rule must be specified deterministically (exact prefix > base-asset prefix > substring > fuzzy) so engineering does not invent it and tests can assert it.
- Specify the maximum rendered result count and the virtualisation threshold so the 50 ms budget is achievable.
- Distinguish three different empty-ish states: catalogue loading, no matches, and matches filtered out by a scope rule - they have different copy.

## Test plan
- Keyboard walkthrough by a designer and by QA/SDET against the spec, including screen-reader dry-run of the combobox semantics.
- Copy review; truncation checks for long symbol names and large volume figures.
- Review against `18-traceability-matrix.md` rows for `US-MKT-001` and `US-MKT-002` to confirm every listed component is either used or explicitly not needed.
- Specification of Playwright-stable test ids for each state, agreed with QA.

## Security notes
- Search must not leak the existence of non-permitted data: results are public instrument metadata only; no account, position or key information appears in any result row for any role.
- Query strings are user input rendered as highlighted text - the spec notes that highlighting must be structural, never HTML injected from the query.
- No exchange credentials or internal endpoint names appear in any state, including error states.

## Accessibility notes
- Full ARIA combobox pattern with `aria-activedescendant` per `SCR-102`; result count announced on change; each option announces symbol, base/quote and recording indicator.
- Per-result actions must be reachable without a pointer and must not require a hover-only affordance.
- Focus is trapped inside the modal while open and restored on close; the quick-switcher must not trap focus.
- Highlight and status chips carry text equivalents.

## Performance notes
- Budget from `US-MKT-002`/`SCR-102`: results within 50 ms of a keystroke with no network call in the common case; the spec forbids per-keystroke layout thrash and mandates virtualised lists beyond the stated threshold.
- Metadata columns (24 h change/volume) are read from the cached ticker snapshot, not subscribed per result; live subscription is limited to visible rows if used at all, and that limit is annotated.

## Observability
- `symbol.searched` and `symbol.search_result_opened` analytics events specified with their properties (query length, result count, rank of selection).
- `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}` specified for each of the three empty-ish states so we can detect a catalogue that is failing to load.

## Definition of Done
- Hi-fi frames for both surfaces, all states, both themes, fully tokenised against E08-D04.
- Interaction/keyboard spec and ranking rule documented and agreed with engineering.
- `14-screens-catalogue.md` `SCR-102`/`SCR-041` design sign-off acceptance checklists all ticked in the ticket.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done), >=2 sprints before the consuming FE story.

- `blocked_by`: E08-D02 (structure), E08-D04 (tokens/components).

title: Hi-fi: SCR-103 symbol info drawer - contract specs and precision rules
body:
## Context
`US-MKT-001` makes the instruments-info cache the single source of precision truth, and `US-MKT-004` requires the same validation rules on client and server with property-based tests. `SCR-103` Symbol info / instrument detail is where those rules become visible to the trader: tick size, lot size, min/max qty, min notional, max leverage, risk-limit tiers, funding interval and next settlement, settlement asset, status - plus CandleViewer-side facts (recording status, coverage start, disk used, retention, pin state).

The design problem is separating three classes of fact that look similar but have very different trust properties: exchange-enforced contract rules (static, authoritative), live market values (subject to staleness), and our own recorder facts (local). Conflating them is how a trader ends up trusting a stale funding countdown.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-103` covering: populated (recorded), populated (not recorded), live block stale/reconnecting, delisted/suspended, catalogue refresh in progress, load error.
- Explicit three-band layout separating contract rules / live values / CandleViewer facts, with the "these rules are enforced by the exchange" note required by the catalogue checklist.
- Components specified: `CMP-036` KeyValueRow (with units), `CMP-046` Drawer, `CMP-125` SymbolInfoPopover, `CMP-126` FundingCountdown, `CMP-177` RecorderStatusRow, `CMP-021` Link, plus the freshness marker from E08-D04.
- Number formatting spec: how tick/lot sizes and min notional are rendered (significant digits, no lossy rounding), and how a precision rule is shown next to an example so the rule is understandable.
- Cross-links: recording status links to the recorder admin screen for Owner only; delisted state links to the chart banner behaviour from E08-D03.

## Out of scope
- The order ticket's own validation UI (`US-MKT-004` enforcement at entry) - owned by the trading epics; this drawer only *explains* the rules.
- Recorder configuration screens (referenced, not designed here).
- Funding/OI analytics views (DERIV epic).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Fact classes are visually separated
  Given the populated drawer
  When reviewed
  Then contract rules, live values and CandleViewer recorder facts occupy distinct labelled bands
  And the exchange-enforcement note appears with the contract rules band

Scenario: Live block degrades without contaminating static facts
  Given the ticker stream for the symbol is stale
  When the drawer is rendered
  Then only the live band carries the stale treatment
  And the contract-rule band remains presented as authoritative

Scenario: Delisted or suspended symbol (edge case)
  Given the instrument status is not Trading
  When the drawer opens
  Then a prominent status explanation is shown, the funding countdown is suppressed rather than counting to a settlement that will not happen, and order-entry entry points are absent

Scenario: Catalogue load failure (failure case)
  Given GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol} fails
  When the drawer opens
  Then an error state explains that contract rules could not be loaded and that order entry is blocked until they are
  And a retry action is offered

Scenario: Precision values are never rounded misleadingly
  Given a tick size such as 0.00001
  When rendered
  Then the full precise value is shown, not a truncated approximation
  And the formatting rule is stated in the spec

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO and accessibility review are complete
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Data sources per the catalogue: `GET /api/v1/instruments/{symbol}` and `GET /api/v1/market/data-coverage?symbol`; live fields subscribe to `ticker.{symbol}` only while the drawer is open (and must unsubscribe on close, respecting the 30 s grace from `US-MKT-005`).
- The funding countdown depends on the clock offset from `US-MKT-009`; the spec must define what the countdown shows when the offset alarm is active (show the warning, do not silently display a possibly-wrong countdown).
- Risk-limit tiers can be a long table - specify collapse/expand and the maximum default height inside a drawer.
- Recorder facts are Owner-relevant; specify the Manager/Viewer variant.

## Test plan
- Review against the `SCR-103` design sign-off acceptance checklist in `14-screens-catalogue.md`, item by item, recorded on the ticket.
- Screen-reader dry run of the description-list structure and units.
- Formatting spec validated against real Bybit instrument fixtures (smallest and largest tick/lot values present in the linear universe).
- QA walkthrough to agree test ids and to confirm each state is reachable in a test environment.

## Security notes
- Recorder facts (disk used, retention, coverage) reveal system internals; the spec defines RBAC visibility (Owner full, Manager limited, Viewer none) so an over-sharing default is not shipped.
- Links to admin screens must be hidden, not merely disabled, for roles without access.
- No API keys, account ids or internal hostnames rendered in any state including errors.

## Accessibility notes
- Facts are a description list with explicit units per `SCR-103`; the contract-rules section uses plain sentences.
- External references are labelled as leaving the app.
- The countdown is a live region updated at <=1 Hz with a text alternative ("funding in 3 h 12 m"), and is not announced continuously.
- Drawer follows the standard dialog focus rules from the design system (focus moves in, is trapped, restores on close).

## Performance notes
- Static metadata is cached; the drawer must open without a network round-trip when the catalogue is warm.
- Only the live band subscribes; subscription is torn down on close.
- Countdown updates <=1 Hz; risk-limit table virtualised or collapsed if long.

## Observability
- `symbol.info_viewed` analytics event specified.
- Error state emits an event distinguishing catalogue-load failure from coverage-load failure so we can tell which dependency broke.

## Definition of Done
- Frames for all states in both themes, tokenised against E08-D04.
- Formatting and RBAC visibility rules documented; catalogue checklist fully ticked.
- `14-screens-catalogue.md` `SCR-103` updated where the design diverged.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done), >=2 sprints ahead of the consuming FE story.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E08-D04 (data-confidence tokens and state set must be published before this drawer is specified).
- Consumes contract-spec field semantics from `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/api/v1/instruments/{symbol}` and the instrument cache shape delivered by E08-S01.
