title: Hi-fi: SCR-100 watchlist panel & SCR-101 manager with live-column states
body:
## Context
The watchlist is the highest-density consumer of E08's ticker fan-out: `US-MKT-003` requires live last price, 24 h %, 24 h volume, funding, next-funding countdown and OI change for up to 200 symbols, driven by **one batched tickers subscription** with <=10 topics per subscribe frame, and requires stale cells to grey out with an explicit marker rather than freeze. `SCR-100` additionally caps updates at 4 Hz coalesced and virtualises beyond 60 rows.

This is where the E08-D04 freshness marker gets its hardest test: it must be legible at row density, cheap at 4 Hz across 200 rows, and unambiguous when only *some* columns are stale (e.g. tickers fine, OI feed lagging).

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-100`: populated, loading, empty ("Add symbols to watch"), partially stale (per-column and per-row), fully disconnected, delisted row (struck through with explanation), subscription cap reached ("Watching 200 symbols - remove some to add more"), REC chip states.
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-101` Watchlist manager modal: create/rename/duplicate/delete, reorder (drag plus explicit move up/down buttons), bulk add by paste, import/export, per-list column configuration, delete confirmation, empty state, validation errors (duplicate name, >200 symbols).
- Column spec: which columns are live-subscribed vs derived, sort behaviour, column picker defaults, and the numeric formatting/sign conventions (plus/minus signs per the catalogue a11y note).
- Components: `CMP-011` Tag / Chip, `CMP-026` EmptyState, `CMP-049` Table, `CMP-056` ColumnPicker, `CMP-161` WatchlistRow, `CMP-162` WatchlistGroupTabs, `CMP-001` Button, `CMP-043` Dialog, `CMP-044` ConfirmDialog, `CMP-067` FileDrop.
- Interaction spec: click to set active symbol for the focused sync group, drag onto a panel to rebind, `Del` to remove, right-click menu (record/unrecord Owner-only, open in new chart, add alert, copy symbol).

## Out of scope
- The scanner/screener (`SCR-104`) - E08-D08.
- Recorder administration screens (linked only).
- Alert creation flow (entry point only).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Per-column staleness is expressible
  Given tickers are live but the OI-derived column has not updated within its threshold
  When the row renders
  Then only the affected cells carry the stale marker and the row is not marked wholly stale
  And the spec states the per-column thresholds

Scenario: Frozen values never look live (failure case)
  Given the tickers stream drops for the whole list
  When the panel renders
  Then every live cell is demoted with an explicit stale treatment and the panel-level indicator from E08-D03 is shown
  And no cell retains its live styling

Scenario: Subscription cap
  Given the list already contains 200 symbols
  When the user attempts to add another
  Then the cap state is shown with the exact message and a path to remove symbols
  And the add control communicates the cap before the attempt where possible

Scenario: Reorder without a pointer
  Given a keyboard-only user in SCR-101
  When they reorder a list
  Then explicit move up / move down controls are available and announce the new position

Scenario: Delisted row (edge case)
  Given a symbol is delisted while on a watchlist
  Then the row is struck through with 'Delisted by the exchange', the stale marker is suppressed per the precedence rule, and its chart/order entry points are disabled

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO, accessibility specialist and engineering have reviewed
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Design must respect the subscription model: one batched `ticker.{symbol}` subscription set with <=10 args per subscribe frame, fan-out internally (`US-MKT-005`); the spec forbids any design that implies a per-row independent connection.
- Virtualisation beyond 60 rows means off-screen rows have no subscriptions - the spec must define what an off-screen row shows when scrolled into view (a brief initialising state, not a fabricated value).
- Next-funding countdown per row at 1 Hz would be 200 timers; the spec mandates a single shared clock tick and identical rounding across rows.
- Import/export format for `SCR-101` must be specified (plain symbol list, validation on import, what happens to unknown/delisted symbols on import).

## Test plan
- Density review at the supported density settings with 200 rows of realistic Bybit symbols.
- Screen-reader pass on the ARIA grid, sortable headers and the REC chip text.
- Walkthrough with engineering against the batched subscription constraints and the 4 Hz coalescing budget.
- Both catalogue design sign-off checklists (`SCR-101`) ticked item by item on the ticket.

## Security notes
- Record/unrecord is an Owner-only, audited action (`recorder.auto_record_started`) - the spec must hide, not merely disable, the control for other roles.
- Import accepts a user-supplied file: the spec mandates that imported symbol strings are validated against the instrument catalogue and rendered as text, never interpreted; oversized files are rejected with a clear message.
- Exported files contain only symbol lists - the spec states that no account or key data is ever included.

## Accessibility notes
- Table is a proper ARIA grid with sortable headers and a caption; percentage changes carry explicit plus/minus signs (not colour alone).
- REC chip has a text label; stale markers have text equivalents; announcements are summarised at panel level rather than per-cell to avoid flooding.
- Every action button in `SCR-101` names its target; reorder has non-drag equivalents; delete is a ConfirmDialog.
- Right-click actions are available from a keyboard-accessible menu too.

## Performance notes
- Budget: ticker updates coalesced to 4 Hz; virtualised beyond 60 rows (`SCR-100`).
- Stale marking must be a class toggle on existing cells - no extra DOM per cell, no per-row animation (constraint inherited from E08-D04).
- Countdown driven by one shared timer; sorting must not re-mount rows.

## Observability
- Analytics per catalogue: `watchlist.symbol_added`, `watchlist.symbol_removed`, `watchlist.reordered`, `watchlist.column_changed`, `watchlist.symbol_activated`, `watchlist.created|renamed|deleted|duplicated|imported`; audited `recorder.auto_record_started`.
- `data_confidence.state_entered {surface: SCR-100, state}` so we can measure how often traders see stale data.

## Definition of Done
- All frames and states for both screens in both themes, tokenised against E08-D04.
- Interaction, column, formatting and import/export specs documented.
- Catalogue checklists ticked; `14-screens-catalogue.md` updated on divergence.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done), >=2 sprints ahead of the consuming FE story.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E08-D02 (wireframes fix the staleness/gap vocabulary), E08-D04 (data-confidence tokens and live-cell state set).
- Live-cell update cadence and batching limits come from US-MKT-003 (max 10 topics per subscribe frame) and the ticker fan-out delivered by E08-S03.
- Downstream: E08-D13 handoff, E08-D14 design QA, E08-Q05 E2E/a11y audit of the watchlist; frontend build of SCR-100/SCR-101 is gated on this ticket being Done.

title: Hi-fi: SCR-104 scanner panel - live criteria, caps and estimated metrics
body:
## Context
`SCR-104` Scanner / screener filters the whole USDT-perp universe by live criteria (24 h change, volume, funding rate, OI delta, tape-speed z-score, spread, volatility) against `GET /api/v1/scanner?filters=` on a 5 s cadence, capped at 200 results. It depends on E08's instruments catalogue (`US-MKT-001`) and ticker fan-out (`US-MKT-005`), and it is the first surface that mixes exchange-reported facts with **heuristic, estimated** metrics (tape-speed z-score, regime) that must be flagged with `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge per the `R9 Advice boundary` discipline.

The design risk is that a screener implies precision it does not have; the design must make "estimated" and "only live metrics for non-recorded symbols" unmissable.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-104`: filter bar with the full criteria set, results table with sparklines, no matches, too many matches (capped at 200 with a note), filter validation error ("Minimum must be less than maximum"), scan failed, scan stale/degraded when the underlying feeds are degraded.
- Saved-preset UI: save, rename, delete, apply, default preset, and the copy explaining that presets store criteria, not results.
- Result actions: open chart, add to watchlist, create alert.
- Estimated-metric treatment: `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge in the *filter list itself* (not only on results) and the explanatory note that scanning is limited to live metrics for symbols we are not recording.
- Components: `CMP-011` Tag / Chip, `CMP-024` Sparkline, `CMP-026` EmptyState, `CMP-049` Table, `CMP-055` FilterBar, `CMP-056` ColumnPicker, `CMP-227` EstimatedBadge.

## Out of scope
- The detector algorithms themselves (DET epic) - this design only presents their outputs and flags them as estimated.
- Alert configuration (entry point only).
- Server-side scan implementation and its query language.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Estimated criteria are flagged before use
  Given the filter bar lists tape-speed z-score and regime
  When a user opens the criteria list
  Then those options carry the estimated badge in the option list itself
  And selecting one surfaces a one-line explanation of how it is derived

Scenario: Result cap is explained, not silent
  Given more than 200 instruments match
  When results render
  Then exactly 200 are shown with an explicit note that the result set is capped and how to narrow it
  And sorting is stated to apply to the capped set, not the universe

Scenario: Invalid filter range (failure case)
  Given a minimum greater than the maximum
  When the filter is applied
  Then an inline validation error names the offending filter and the rule
  And the previous result set is retained rather than cleared to an ambiguous empty state

Scenario: Underlying feed degraded (edge case)
  Given the ticker or OI feed is stale
  When a scan returns
  Then results are marked as computed from possibly stale inputs using the E08-D04 vocabulary
  And the scan is not presented as authoritative

Scenario: No matches vs scan failed are distinct
  Given a scan that returns zero rows and a scan that errors
  Then each has its own state and copy, and neither reuses the other's wording

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO and accessibility review are complete
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Per the catalogue, scanning is server-side over the hot tier; the panel polls at <=0.2 Hz or subscribes to a scan topic and **never** evaluates criteria client-side across the universe - annotate this constraint in the spec so no future designer proposes client-side filtering.
- Sparklines must be cheap: specify sample count and that they are static per refresh, not animated.
- Preset storage is per user; specify conflict behaviour if a preset references a criterion later removed.
- Copy must preserve the advice boundary: the scanner surfaces conditions, never recommendations.

## Test plan
- Review against the `SCR-104` design sign-off acceptance checklist, item by item, recorded on the ticket.
- Content review of all estimated-metric explanations by the content reviewer and the Architect (accuracy of the derivation description).
- Screen-reader pass on the filter controls, the result count announcement and the table caption stating the active filter set in plain language.
- Density/perf review with 200 rows and sparklines at the supported densities.

## Security notes
- Scanner results are public market metadata; the spec states that no account-scoped data (positions, PnL) may ever be added as a column without a separate RBAC review.
- Filter values are user input echoed into the table caption - spec requires text rendering, no interpretation.
- Presets are user-scoped; the spec forbids cross-user preset visibility.

## Accessibility notes

title: Hi-fi: SCR-147 exchange connectivity, rate limits and clock skew
body:
## Context
E08 introduces the parts of the system most likely to fail quietly: the Bybit REST client with its error taxonomy (including rate-limit `10018`), the subscription manager with its <=10-args-per-request budget, sequence-gap detection and resubscribe, and the clock-offset measurement required by `US-MKT-009` (re-measured every 5 minutes, alarm above 500 ms drift). `SCR-147` Admin: exchange connectivity & rate limits is the Owner-facing surface where all of that becomes inspectable, and it is the screen the Owner will open first when something feels wrong.

It is RBAC-gated inside the web app (there is no separate admin app), rendered in `CMP-087` AdminLayout, and per the catalogue it includes a fan-out budget simulator ("a 5-account fan-out with brackets costs about 15 requests - 9 % of your minute budget"). E08 only needs the market-data half to be real in R0, but the screen must be designed whole so later epics slot in without redesign.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for `SCR-147`: healthy, approaching limit, throttled, banned with the exchange's stated recovery time, WS disconnected, resubscribe storm, clock-skew warning and alarm, historical usage view, and a data-unavailable state (our own metrics pipeline down).
- Per-endpoint-class table (REST order, REST query, public WS, private WS) with limit, current usage, window and headroom as numbers with units, per-account rows labelled by account.
- Subscription inspector for E08: active topics per connection, args-per-request budget consumption, gap counter, last resubscribe, last snapshot re-seed per symbol.
- Clock-skew indicator: current offset, last measurement time, next measurement, alarm state at >500 ms, and the copy explaining consequences (bar boundaries, signatures).
- Force-reconnect action with confirmation, marked as audited (`connectivity.reconnect_forced`), and the request-budget change control (`connectivity.budget_changed`, audited).
- Historical usage sparkline **with a table alternative** (catalogue requirement).
- Components: `CMP-023` Progress Bar, `CMP-024` Sparkline, `CMP-036` KeyValueRow, `CMP-049` Table, `CMP-087` AdminLayout, `CMP-178` SystemHealthTile, `CMP-044` ConfirmDialog, `CMP-093` AuditActionTrigger.

## Out of scope
- Private/order endpoints' real data (arrives with the OMS epics) - designed as placeholders with the layout reserved.
- The general system-health screen and maintenance mode (other epics).
- Alerting/notification routing for these conditions (observability epic) - only the on-screen state is designed.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Budget consumption is legible as numbers, not just bars
  Given any endpoint class row
  When rendered
  Then limit, current usage, window and headroom appear as explicit numbers with units alongside any progress bar
  And the bar is never the only representation

Scenario: Throttled and banned are distinct and actionable (failure case)
  Given the adapter has received a 10018 rate-limit error
  When the screen renders
  Then a throttled state names the endpoint class, the observed limit and the recovery time the exchange stated
  And a banned state is visually and textually distinct from throttled, with what the operator may and may not do

Scenario: Clock drift alarm
  Given the measured offset to Bybit server time exceeds 500 ms
  When the screen renders
  Then the skew indicator is in its alarm state with the offset value, the measurement age and the stated consequences
  And a re-measure action is offered

Scenario: Force reconnect is deliberate and audited
  Given the Owner triggers Force reconnect
  Then a confirmation states exactly what will be interrupted (subscriptions dropped and re-established, brief resync on dependent panels)
  And the action is marked as written to the audit log

Scenario: Our own metrics are unavailable (edge case)
  Given the backend cannot report its rate-limit counters
  When the screen renders
  Then it shows an explicit unknown state rather than zeros
  And zeros are never shown as if they meant 'no usage'

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO, the Security engineer and accessibility review are complete
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Usage figures come from the backend's own accounting plus exchange response headers, sampled at 1 Hz; the browser never queries the exchange directly (catalogue constraint) - annotate it so no one proposes a direct call.
- The subscription inspector must be designed for realistic scale: dozens of topics across a few connections; specify grouping (by connection, then by topic type) and virtualisation threshold.
- Show the <=10 args/request subscribe budget explicitly, because it is a real constraint of the Bybit adapter and an operator needs to see when it is the bottleneck.
- Distinguish three failure origins in the UI: exchange-side (rate limit, 5xx, maintenance), network-side (disconnect), and our side (bus backpressure, bounded-queue drops from M5). Each has different operator action.

## Test plan
- Review against the `SCR-147` design sign-off acceptance checklist, item by item, recorded on the ticket.
- Walkthrough with the E08 engineering lead confirming every displayed figure maps to a metric the adapter actually exports.
- Security review of the RBAC and content exposure (below) recorded by the Security engineer.
- Screen-reader pass on the per-endpoint table and the alarm states; table-alternative for the sparkline verified.

## Security notes
- The screen is Owner-gated via `CMP-087` AdminLayout; Manager/Viewer must not see it at all, and its route must not be discoverable in navigation for those roles.
- No API key material, key ids beyond a masked label, or signed request contents may appear; account rows are labelled with the account alias, not credentials.
- Force-reconnect and budget-change are audited actions and must use `CMP-093` AuditActionTrigger with typed/explicit confirmation per the admin pattern.
- Raw exchange error bodies are mapped to error classes before display, preventing incidental leakage of request metadata.

## Accessibility notes
- Per the catalogue: a per-endpoint-class table with limit, usage, window and headroom as numbers with units; per-account rows labelled with the account.
- Alarm states use `role="alert"` once on entry, not repeatedly; degraded states use `role="status"`.
- The historical sparkline has an equivalent data table toggle (mandated by the catalogue checklist).
- Progress bars expose `aria-valuenow`/`aria-valuetext` with the real numbers and units.

## Performance notes
- Sampling at 1 Hz; the spec forbids animated bars and mandates that the table updates in place without re-mounting rows.
- Subscription inspector virtualised beyond the stated row threshold.
- Historical view fetches on demand, not on every sample tick.

## Observability
- `connectivity.panel_viewed` (analytics); `connectivity.budget_changed` and `connectivity.reconnect_forced` (audited) - specified with their payloads.
- The design names the metrics it depends on so E08 engineering exports them: per-topic last-message age, gap counter, resubscribe counter, snapshot re-seed counter, rate-limit-error counter by class, clock offset gauge, bus queue depth and drop counter.

## Definition of Done
- All frames and states in both themes, tokenised against E08-D04; redlines complete.
- Metric-to-display mapping agreed with engineering and listed on the ticket.
- Security review comment recorded; catalogue checklist ticked; `14-screens-catalogue.md` `SCR-147` updated on divergence.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done), >=2 sprints ahead of the consuming FE story.

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E08-D02 (connection-state vocabulary), E08-D04 (data-confidence tokens).

- Downstream: E08-D13 handoff, E08-D14 design QA, E08-T06 observability wiring; frontend build of SCR-147 is gated on this ticket being Done.

title: Hi-fi: SCR-151 empty/backfill states for history, coverage and gaps
body:
## Context
`US-MKT-008` (historical OHLCV backfill) introduces states no other epic has yet: bars paging from `/v5/market/kline` with visible progress, a cache-hit fast path, and a rate-limited path that must keep the partial result usable and show "loading older bars..." **without blocking interaction**. `US-MKT-006` adds gapped windows after a sequence gap and REST recent-trade backfill. `SCR-151` Empty state pattern is the catalogued home for these: its mandated anatomy is a heading stating the fact, one sentence of cause, one primary action, one secondary learn-more link, plus the recorder explanation where relevant.

The design contribution here is the distinction between "nothing exists", "nothing matches your filter" and "we have not recorded this yet / we are fetching it now" - three states that are routinely conflated and that mean completely different things to a trader deciding whether to trust a chart.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Hi-fi frames for the `SCR-151` variants owned by E08:
  - `variant="backfill-in-progress"` - paging progress with bars-loaded/target, partial data usable underneath, non-blocking.
  - `variant="backfill-throttled"` - rate-limited, backing off, partial result retained, no blocking spinner.
  - `variant="recording-not-started"` - data not recorded yet, carrying the recording-start timestamp (catalogue requirement).
  - `variant="coverage-gap"` - a gapped window inside otherwise-good data, with what is missing and why.
  - `variant="nothing-created-yet"` and `variant="no-filter-matches"` - the two non-E08 classes, designed here because the pattern must be complete and consistent.
- The in-context (non-full-panel) treatment: how a gapped window is marked *inside* a populated surface rather than replacing it, referencing the E08-D04 vocabulary.
- Copy for each class, content-reviewed, including the role-aware variant (action button vs explicit "no action is available to this role").
- Components: `CMP-001` Button, `CMP-019` Icon, `CMP-021` Link, `CMP-026` EmptyState, `CMP-023` Progress Bar.

## Out of scope
- The chart's own rendering of gapped ranges on the price/time axis (chart-engine epic consumes this spec but designs its own canvas treatment).
- Replay coverage states (replay epic).
- Recorder configuration UI.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Three empty classes are never conflated
  Given the pattern spec
  When each of nothing-created-yet, no-filter-matches and data-not-recorded-yet is rendered
  Then each has distinct copy naming its own cause
  And no variant uses a bare 'No data'

Scenario: Backfill does not block interaction
  Given a chart is backfilling older bars
  When the backfill state renders
  Then already-loaded bars remain visible and interactive
  And the progress indicator is non-modal and does not cover the data

Scenario: Rate-limited backfill (failure case)
  Given the exchange returns a rate-limit error during paging
  Then the state explains that older bars are still loading and are being retried
  And the partial result is explicitly labelled as partial rather than presented as complete history

Scenario: Recorded-coverage state carries a timestamp (edge case)
  Given a surface that requires recorded data which began at a known time
  When the recording-not-started variant renders
  Then it states the recording-start timestamp
  And, for roles that cannot start recording, it states that no action is available to them instead of showing a dead button

Scenario: Gap inside populated data
  Given a sequence gap occurred in the middle of an otherwise good window
  Then the gap is marked in context using the data-confidence vocabulary rather than emptying the whole surface

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given CDO and accessibility review are complete
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Per `US-MKT-008`, target is <=300 ms to first paint from cache for 5 000 bars - the design must therefore avoid a loading state in the cache-hit path entirely; specify that the cache-hit path shows data, never a skeleton.
- Paging respects the exchange's 1 000-row limit with jittered retry; progress must be expressed in a way that tolerates an unknown total (bars loaded + target days, not a false percentage).
- Empty states must render without initialising heavy resources (no GL context, no subscriptions) per the catalogue performance note.
- Specify the transition from empty -> populated so a surface does not flash an empty state during a fast load (minimum delay before showing an empty/loading state).

## Test plan
- Review against the `SCR-151` design sign-off acceptance checklist, item by item, recorded on the ticket.
- Copy review for all classes; explicit check that no variant reads as blaming the user.
- Screen-reader pass: heading structure, announcement on entering an empty state, and that the cause sentence is part of the accessible description.
- Walkthrough with engineering on the transition thresholds so the anti-flash rule is implementable.

## Security notes
- Empty/error copy must not reveal internal causes (endpoint names, stack traces, exchange raw payloads); causes are expressed in user terms with a role-gated diagnostic path only for the Owner.
- The role-aware variant must not disclose that an action exists for other roles beyond a neutral statement.

## Accessibility notes
- Catalogue mandate: a heading, one sentence naming the cause, and either an action or an explicit statement that no action is available to this role; never an icon alone.
- Progress must expose `aria-valuetext` in human terms ("loaded 3 200 of about 5 000 bars") or, when the total is unknown, an indeterminate state with a text description.
- Entering an empty state is announced once via a status region; repeated re-entry within a short window is not re-announced.

## Performance notes
- Empty states cost nothing: no GL context, no subscriptions (catalogue requirement) - stated in the spec as an implementation constraint.
- Progress updates at <=2 Hz; no animated skeletons on the cache-hit path.
- Anti-flash minimum-delay rule specified numerically.

## Observability
- `empty_state_shown {surface, reason}` per the catalogue, with `reason` drawn from a closed enumeration matching the variants defined here so the data is analysable.
- Backfill states emit start/finish/throttled events so we can measure how often traders wait and for how long.

## Definition of Done
- All variants in both themes, tokenised against E08-D04; copy final.
- Reason enumeration agreed with engineering and analytics.
- Catalogue checklist ticked; `14-screens-catalogue.md` `SCR-151` updated on divergence.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done), >=2 sprints ahead of the consuming FE story.

## Dependencies

- Downstream: E08-D13 handoff, E08-D14 design QA; frontend build of SCR-151 is gated on this ticket being Done.

title: Motion spec: connection transitions, resync and freshness without strobing
body:
## Context
Every E08 state is *transient by nature*: a socket drops and recovers, a book invalidates and re-seeds, a cell goes stale and returns. Without a deliberate motion spec, these transitions become the most annoying and least trustworthy part of the product - banners popping in and out during a flapping connection, 200 watchlist rows fading simultaneously, a resync overlay strobing on every snapshot.

Motion here is not decoration; it is the mechanism that makes a state change *noticed once* rather than *noticed constantly*, and it interacts directly with the render-performance risk (`R2`) because these surfaces update at 4 Hz (watchlist) up to tape/DOM rates.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Motion spec added to the design system (`16-design-system-brief.md` motion section) covering:
  - Banner appear/dismiss for `SCR-152` (duration, easing, direction, minimum visible duration, debounce before reappearance).
  - Panel-level resync overlay fade for `SCR-050`, `SCR-053`, `SCR-100`.
  - Cell freshness transition for `CMP-161` WatchlistRow and `CMP-036` KeyValueRow live fields - a single settle transition, not a pulse.
  - Value-change emphasis (tick up/down) and its explicit interaction with staleness: a stale cell never animates.
  - Backfill progress motion for the `SCR-151` variants.
- Hysteresis/debounce table: minimum durations and cool-downs per state so a flapping feed cannot produce a strobing UI.
- `prefers-reduced-motion` specification for every transition: the reduced variant must still communicate the state change (instant style change plus text), never simply removing the signal.
- Prototype(s) demonstrating the flapping-connection case and the 200-row watchlist case for review.

## Out of scope
- Chart-canvas animation (pan/zoom/series transitions) - chart-engine epic.
- Onboarding or marketing motion.
- Motion for trading actions (order placed/filled) - trading epics.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Flapping connection cannot strobe
  Given the connection drops and recovers five times within ten seconds
  When the banner behaviour follows the hysteresis table
  Then the banner is shown at most once per cool-down window
  And it remains visible for at least its minimum duration before dismissing

Scenario: Stale cells do not animate
  Given a watchlist cell enters the stale state
  When its transition plays
  Then it settles into the stale style once and performs no ongoing animation
  And no value-change emphasis can play while the cell is stale

Scenario: Reduced motion preserves meaning (edge case)
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is set
  When any E08 state change occurs
  Then the change is applied without animation but remains perceivable via style and text
  And no state becomes invisible as a result

Scenario: Mass transition stays within budget (failure case)
  Given 200 watchlist rows all become stale in the same frame
  When the specified transition is applied
  Then the spec's technique keeps the work compositor-friendly and bounded
  And the prototype demonstrates it without dropping below the frame budget on the reference machine

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given the motion designer, accessibility specialist, CDO and a front-end engineer have reviewed
  Then blocking comments are resolved and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Restrict animated properties to `opacity` and `transform` so transitions are compositor-only; explicitly forbid animating colour on hot surfaces where a mass transition can occur, or specify it only for the small-N case.
- Express every timing as a design token (duration + easing) so engineering consumes tokens rather than transcribing numbers.
- The value-change emphasis must be cancellable and must degrade gracefully when updates arrive faster than the animation duration (latest-wins, no queueing).
- Hysteresis values should be derived from the thresholds researched in E08-D01, not invented independently.

## Test plan
- Prototype review of the two hard cases (flapping connection, mass staleness).
- Reduced-motion audit of every specified transition.
- Front-end feasibility review confirming the properties chosen are compositor-only and that the mass case is achievable within the frame budget.
- Specification of the performance assertion QA will later run (frame budget during a forced mass-stale event).

## Security notes
- No security surface directly; however the spec must forbid motion that delays the appearance of a safety-critical message - the disconnected banner's "trading is disabled" must be readable immediately, so its entrance duration is capped.

## Accessibility notes
- Full `prefers-reduced-motion` coverage with meaning preserved (above).
- No flashing faster than the WCAG three-flashes-per-second threshold anywhere in the spec; the hysteresis table is the mechanism that guarantees it.
- Motion must never be the only indication of a state change; text/style always accompanies it.
- Announcement timing is coordinated with motion so screen-reader output does not precede or contradict the visual state.

## Performance notes
- Budget stated against `06-performance-and-load-standard.md`: state transitions must not cause the watchlist (200 rows) or the app shell to drop frames; only compositor-friendly properties animate.
- Mass transitions are specified as a single class change on a container where possible, rather than per-element animations.
- No transition may run continuously; all are one-shot.

## Observability
- Recommend counting suppressed banner appearances (hysteresis hits) so we can tell the difference between "the connection was fine" and "the connection flapped but we hid it".

## Definition of Done
- Motion tokens and the hysteresis table merged into `16-design-system-brief.md`; prototypes linked.
- Reduced-motion variants specified for every transition.
- Front-end feasibility confirmed; performance assertion agreed with QA.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done).

## Dependencies
- `blocked_by`: E08-D03 (hi-fi banner and per-panel badge states are the frames this motion spec animates), E08-D04 (token set incl. duration/easing tokens).
- Must respect the reduced-motion requirements in `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md` and the frame-budget ceiling in `docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md`; transitions may not run on the chart render thread.
- Downstream: E08-D12 (a11y design review), E08-D13 handoff, E08-D14 design QA.

title: Accessibility design review of all E08 market-data surfaces
body:
## Context
`05-accessibility-standard.md` requires WCAG 2.2 AA across the product, and `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` gates Story DoD on axe-core CI plus manual screen-reader passes. Catching a11y defects at implementation time is expensive; catching them in the design is cheap. E08's surfaces are unusually a11y-hostile: dense live tables, transient status changes, colour-coded confidence states, and a screen-reader flooding risk from constantly updating values.

This ticket is the single formal accessibility design review across everything E08 designs, performed **before** handoff so findings are fixed in the source of truth rather than patched in code.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Structured review of: `SCR-152` (E08-D03), `SCR-102`/`SCR-041` (E08-D05), `SCR-103` (E08-D06), `SCR-100`/`SCR-101` (E08-D07), `SCR-104` (E08-D08), `SCR-147` (E08-D09), `SCR-151` (E08-D10), plus the motion spec (E08-D11) and the design-system contribution (E08-D04).
- Per-surface checklist covering: semantic structure (grid vs table vs list), accessible names and descriptions, focus order and visible focus, keyboard equivalents for every pointer-only interaction (drag-to-rebind, right-click menus, drag reorder), live-region strategy and flood control, contrast in both themes at all states, non-colour redundancy, reduced-motion, target sizes, and `SCR-151`'s no-bare-'No data' rule.
- A **live-region budget**: which surfaces may announce, at what maximum rate, and which use polite summaries rather than per-update announcements - this is the single highest-risk a11y issue in a real-time product.
- Findings log with severity (blocker / major / minor), owner and target ticket; blockers must be fixed in the originating design ticket before its sign-off stands.
- Screen-reader script for the manual passes QA will run later (NVDA/VoiceOver steps per surface), handed to QA as the basis of the implementation-time pass.

## Out of scope
- Running axe-core against built code (implementation-time activity in the consuming stories).
- Remediating the findings (done in the originating design tickets).
- Chart-canvas accessibility (chart-engine epic has its own review; E08 only covers the confidence layer on top).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every E08 surface reviewed against the standard
  Given the checklist
  When the review completes
  Then every surface listed in scope has a completed checklist with a pass/fail per item
  And every fail has a severity, an owner and a linked design ticket

Scenario: Live-region flooding is prevented by design
  Given a surface whose values update several times per second
  When its live-region strategy is reviewed
  Then it uses a rate-limited summary rather than per-value announcements
  And the maximum announcement rate is stated numerically

Scenario: Pointer-only interaction found (failure case)
  Given a design relies on drag-and-drop or right-click alone
  When the review runs
  Then it is recorded as a blocker
  And the originating design ticket is reopened until a keyboard equivalent is specified

Scenario: Contrast failure at a degraded state (edge case)
  Given the stale treatment reduces contrast below AA in one theme
  Then it is recorded as a blocker and corrected in E08-D04 tokens
  And the corrected value is re-verified before sign-off

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given all blockers are closed and majors are either closed or accepted with a recorded rationale
  Then the accessibility specialist and the CDO record sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Review the *specifications*, not just the pixels: an accessible name written in a redline is what engineering will implement, so missing names are findings.
- Use the recorded Bybit fixture densities for contrast and legibility checks so the review reflects real content lengths (long symbol names, large volume numbers).
- Verify the confidence vocabulary survives in a screen-reader-only experience: a blind user must be able to tell live from stale from gapped without seeing the styling.

## Test plan
- Two reviewers: the accessibility specialist plus one product designer not involved in the original designs.
- Automated contrast pass over the exported tokens for every state/theme pair.
- Screen-reader dry runs against the interactive prototypes where they exist.
- Findings re-verified after remediation before this ticket closes.

## Security notes
- Accessible descriptions must not expose role-gated diagnostic content (e.g. the Owner-only `Details` payload on `SCR-152`) to roles that cannot see it visually - the review explicitly checks that `aria-describedby` content follows the same RBAC filtering as the visual content.

## Accessibility notes
- This ticket *is* the accessibility work; its own output is the checklist, the live-region budget and the screen-reader script.
- Standard applied: WCAG 2.2 AA per `05-accessibility-standard.md`, including 2.2-specific criteria (focus appearance, dragging movements alternative, target size) which are directly relevant to the watchlist drag interactions.

## Performance notes
- The live-region budget is also a performance constraint: unbounded announcements are expensive for assistive tech; the budget is expressed so it can be enforced in code.
- Any remediation that would require per-cell DOM additions is flagged against the E08-D04 performance clause and an alternative is sought.

## Observability
- Findings log kept as a durable artefact linked from the epic so the implementation-time a11y passes can verify the same items.
- Recommend an axe-core rule set per surface for CI, listed on the ticket.

## Definition of Done
- Checklists complete for every in-scope surface; findings log published with severities and owners.
- All blockers closed; majors closed or formally accepted with rationale.
- Live-region budget and screen-reader script handed to QA and attached to E08-D13.
- Accessibility specialist and CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done).

title: Handoff pack for E08 market-data surfaces (specs, tokens, states, test ids)
body:
## Context
The design-ahead rule means E08's front-end stories in Sprint 02-04 must be startable without a designer in the room. `02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.1 requires, before a UI Story is Ready, that the linked design is Done, that components come from `15-component-catalogue.md`, and that **states are enumerated** (empty, loading, error, populated, edge-density). This ticket produces the single artefact that satisfies those requirements for every E08 surface, so that ingestion engineers - who are mostly backend-leaning - can build the client-visible parts correctly.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- A handoff pack covering `SCR-041`, `SCR-100`, `SCR-101`, `SCR-102`, `SCR-103`, `SCR-104`, `SCR-147`, `SCR-151`, `SCR-152` containing, per surface:
  - Frame links (light/dark, all states, all densities) and redlines with token names only - no raw values.
  - **State enumeration table**: state name, trigger condition expressed in backend terms (last-message age, gap detected, resync in progress, backfill in progress, clock offset, delisted, cap reached), precedence, and the copy string.
  - Component list mapped to `15-component-catalogue.md` IDs, with any E08-contributed entries from E08-D04 called out as new.
  - Keyboard map and focus order.
  - Accessible names/descriptions, live-region strategy and announcement rate limits (from E08-D12).
  - Motion tokens applied (from E08-D11), including reduced-motion behaviour.
  - Performance constraints per surface (4 Hz coalescing, virtualisation thresholds, no per-cell DOM, compositor-only animation).
  - **Stable test identifiers** per state, agreed with QA, for Playwright and for analytics.
- Final copy deck: every string in one place, content-reviewed, with variable slots defined (counts, timings, symbol names) and pluralisation rules.
- A "what engineering must ask about" list: the handful of decisions deliberately left to implementation, with the constraint each must satisfy.
- A recorded walkthrough session with the E08 engineering lead and the front-end engineers picking up the Sprint 02-04 stories.

## Out of scope
- Producing new design decisions - anything missing is raised against the originating design ticket, not invented here.
- Implementation code, storybook stories or fixtures (engineering deliverables).
- Surfaces owned by other epics that merely consume the confidence layer.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: A story can enter Ready without a designer
  Given an E08 front-end story referencing a surface in the pack
  When its DoR is checked against 02-definition-of-ready-done.md §3.1
  Then the linked design is Done, all states are enumerated, and every component maps to a catalogue ID
  And no DoR item requires a conversation with the designer to satisfy

Scenario: Every visual state has a backend trigger
  Given the state enumeration table
  When each state is inspected
  Then it names the condition the backend emits or the client computes, in terms engineering can implement
  And any state without such a condition is either removed or escalated as a gap

Scenario: Copy is complete (failure case)
  Given the copy deck
  When searched for placeholders
  Then no lorem, TBD or untranslated placeholder remains
  And every string with a variable defines the variable and its formatting

Scenario: Tokens only, no raw values (edge case)
  Given any redline
  When inspected
  Then colours, spacing, type and motion appear as token names
  And any raw value present is corrected before the pack is published

Scenario: Walkthrough happened and questions were answered
  Given the walkthrough session
  Then open questions raised in it are answered in the pack or tracked with an owner and a date
  And the recording/notes are linked from this ticket

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given the CDO, the E08 engineering lead and QA have reviewed the pack
  Then it is published and the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Express triggers in the same vocabulary the adapter uses (M3/M4 error taxonomy, M5 bus backpressure, M6/M7 book resync) so there is no translation step at implementation time.
- Include the RBAC matrix per surface (Owner/Manager/Viewer) so role-gating is not rediscovered per story.
- Where a surface is only partly in R0 scope (e.g. `SCR-147` private-endpoint rows), mark clearly what is designed-but-not-yet-built so engineers do not implement out-of-scope sections.

## Test plan
- Dry-run the DoR checklist against two real E08 front-end stories using only the pack; any gap found is a defect of this ticket.
- QA reviews the test-id list and confirms each state is reachable and assertable.
- Content reviewer signs off the copy deck.
- Spot-check that every catalogue design sign-off checklist item for the in-scope screens is evidenced in the pack.

## Security notes
- The pack documents, per surface, which content is role-gated and which must never be rendered (raw exchange payloads, key material, internal hostnames, account identifiers beyond aliases) - so the rule ships with the spec rather than living only in a reviewer's head.
- The pack itself contains no secrets, no real account data and no production endpoints; fixture data only.

## Accessibility notes
- The pack carries the E08-D12 outputs verbatim: accessible names, focus orders, live-region budget, screen-reader script, reduced-motion behaviour.
- Each state row includes its announcement policy, so an engineer implementing a state cannot miss it.
- The pack states the axe-core rule set expected to pass per surface.

## Performance notes
- Per-surface budgets restated: watchlist 4 Hz coalesced and virtualised beyond 60 rows; symbol search results within 50 ms with no network call; scanner refresh <=0.2 Hz with a <=3 s full-universe scan; empty states initialise no GL context or subscriptions.

title: Design QA of the implemented E08 market-data surfaces
body:
## Context
`02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes `design-qa` default-on for net-new UI Stories: the built screen is compared against the design spec (spacing, tokens, type, colour, states) by a designer or design-system-trained reviewer, and discrepancies are either fixed or filed as prioritised follow-up bugs. E08 ships the first live-data surfaces in the product, and its most important states (stale, reconnecting, resyncing, gapped, throttled) are precisely the ones engineers cannot easily see during normal development - they only appear when something breaks. Without a deliberate design-QA pass that *forces* those states, they will ship wrong.

## Scope / Deliverables (real IDs)
- Design QA pass over the implemented surfaces: `SCR-041`, `SCR-100`, `SCR-101`, `SCR-102`, `SCR-103`, `SCR-104`, `SCR-147`, `SCR-151`, `SCR-152`.
- **Forced-state matrix**: for each confidence and failure state, the exact way to induce it in a test environment (kill the upstream WS, inject a sequence gap into a recorded fixture, force a `10018` rate-limit response, skew the clock beyond 500 ms, empty the instrument cache, exceed the 200-symbol cap, delist a fixture symbol) - produced jointly with QA/SDET so it is reusable for regression.
- Comparison report per surface: token fidelity (colour/spacing/type/motion), state completeness, copy fidelity, focus/keyboard behaviour, reduced-motion behaviour, both themes, supported densities.
- Defect list with severity and `priority/*`, each either fixed within the epic or filed as a follow-up Bug linked to the originating story.
- Design-system adoption check: any surface using a local style instead of an E08-D04 token is recorded as a defect, not accepted.
- Visual-regression baselines captured for the confidence states so future epics cannot silently drift.

## Out of scope
- Functional correctness of ingestion (covered by the epic's engineering and QA tickets) - design QA reports what is rendered, not whether the data is right.
- Re-designing anything; deviations either become defects or, if the design was wrong, a change request against the originating design ticket.
- Performance benchmarking (engineering perf tickets) beyond observing obvious jank in the reviewed states.

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every designed state is verified against a forced instance
  Given the forced-state matrix
  When the pass completes
  Then each state in the E08-D13 enumeration has been induced and compared against its frame
  And any state that could not be induced is recorded with the reason and a follow-up to make it inducible

Scenario: Token drift is caught
  Given a rendered surface
  When inspected against the published tokens
  Then any colour, spacing, type or motion value not resolving to a token is filed as a defect
  And the defect names the correct token

Scenario: A frozen value ships looking live (failure case)
  Given the upstream feed is killed in the test environment
  When the watchlist is observed
  Then any cell retaining its live styling is filed as a priority/p0 defect
  And the epic cannot be signed off while it is open

Scenario: Reduced motion and both themes are covered (edge case)
  Given prefers-reduced-motion is enabled and the dark theme is active
  When the states are re-checked
  Then the pass covers this combination explicitly
  And defects found only in this combination are filed like any other

Scenario: Sign-off
  Given all p0/p1 design defects are closed and the remainder are filed with owners and priorities
  Then the CDO records sign-off
```

## Technical notes / design
- Run against a build with recorded Bybit fixtures so densities and update rates are realistic, and so the pass is repeatable.
- Use the stable test ids from E08-D13 to script the forced states where possible; the goal is a repeatable procedure, not a one-off manual sweep.
- Check the composition rules explicitly: estimated + stale, delisted + stale, reconnecting + backfilling - these are exactly where implementations diverge from precedence rules.
- Verify the RBAC content split on `SCR-152` `Details` and `SCR-147` by running the pass as each role, not only as Owner.

## Test plan
- Two reviewers: a product designer and a design-system-trained reviewer; QA/SDET assists with inducing states.
- Each surface checked in light and dark, at every supported density, keyboard-only once, and with reduced motion once.
- Screen-reader spot-check of the announcements against the E08-D12 live-region budget (flood check: watch that a flapping feed does not produce continuous speech).
- Visual-regression baselines committed and wired into CI so the states are protected going forward.

## Security notes
- Verify by observation that no role sees content it must not: run the pass as Manager and Viewer and confirm the absence (not mere disabling) of Owner-only diagnostics, record/unrecord controls and admin links.
- Confirm that no error state renders a raw exchange payload, endpoint, key fragment or account identifier - any occurrence is a `priority/p0` security-adjacent defect routed to the Security engineer as well.

## Accessibility notes
- Confirm the axe-core rule set from E08-D13 is green on each surface and that manual keyboard and screen-reader checks match the specified names, focus order and announcement policy.
- Verify WCAG 2.2 items the designs relied on: focus appearance, dragging-movement alternatives on the watchlist, target sizes in dense tables.
- Contrast re-measured in the *rendered* product for the degraded states, not only in the design file.

## Performance notes
- Observe the specified budgets during the pass: watchlist behaviour with 200 rows at 4 Hz, symbol search responsiveness, scanner refresh, and the mass-stale transition from E08-D11; obvious violations are filed and routed to the engineering perf ticket.
- Confirm that empty states initialise no GL context or subscriptions, per the `SCR-151` constraint.

## Observability
- Confirm the analytics/audit events from the E08-D13 table actually fire with the specified payloads during the pass (spot-check via the dev tooling), since missing instrumentation is invisible later.
- Record how many defects were state-related versus token-related, as an input to the epic retro.

## Definition of Done
- All in-scope surfaces reviewed in both themes, all densities, keyboard-only and reduced-motion; forced-state matrix executed.
- Defects filed with severity and priority; p0/p1 closed within the epic.
- Visual-regression baselines committed; adoption check complete with no unauthorised local styles.
- CDO sign-off recorded; Status **Done** (CDO sign-off = Status Done). This ticket is a prerequisite for the E08 epic's own DoD.

title: Black-box test plan for the E08 market-data and ingestion story groups
body:
## Context
E08 is the single market-data path that nine downstream epics consume (`docs/plan/30-release-roadmap.md` §11: `E08 -> {E12, E16, E17, E22, E24, E29}` plus the recorder/replay chain). A defect here does not show up as a broken screen — it shows up as a chart that is *quietly wrong*, which is risk **R7 Data accuracy** and the single worst failure mode in the product. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 requires a written black-box test plan per feature, and `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 makes a recorded QA sign-off non-skippable for every Story in this epic.

No such artefact exists today: the engineering tickets (`E08-T01..T06`, `E08-S01..S07`) each state what to build, but there is nothing a QA engineer can execute end-to-end against a staging build wired to the recorded fixture corpus (`E08-T05`) to declare "market data behaves as specified". This ticket produces it.

It is deliberately **black-box**: written against the observable surface — REST endpoints in `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml`, WS topics in `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1, screens `SCR-100..104`, `SCR-041`, `SCR-152`, and the Prometheus metrics/health endpoints — with no knowledge of internal helpers, so it survives the refactors that `E08-T06` and E17 will inevitably cause.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `qa/plans/e08-market-data-test-plan.md`, organised into six executable groups mirroring the story structure:
  1. **Instrument catalogue & search** (US-MKT-001, US-MKT-002; `E08-S01`) — `GET /instruments`, `GET /instruments/{symbol}`, `POST /instruments/refresh`, `SCR-102`, `SCR-041`, `SCR-103`.
  2. **Precision & filter validation** (US-MKT-004; `E08-S02`) — shared rounding rule source, violation codes `PRICE_NOT_TICK_MULTIPLE`, `QTY_NOT_LOT_MULTIPLE`, `QTY_BELOW_MIN`, `QTY_ABOVE_MAX`, `NOTIONAL_BELOW_MIN`, `SYMBOL_NOT_TRADING`.
  3. **Live ticker stream** (US-MKT-005; `E08-S03`) — WS `ticker.{symbol}` and batched `ticker`, `GET /instruments/{symbol}/ticker`, `SCR-100`, `SCR-101`, `SCR-104`.
  4. **Tape ingestion** (US-MKT-006; `E08-S04`) — WS `trades.{symbol}`, `GET /market/trades`, ordering, dedup, gap detection.
  5. **Order-book reconstruction** (US-MKT-007; `E08-S05`) — WS `book.{symbol}.{depth}`, `GET /market/orderbook`, snapshot+delta, sequence-gap → invalidate → resync, crossed-book rejection.
  6. **Historical backfill & clock sync** (US-MKT-008, US-MKT-009; `E08-S06`, `E08-S07`) — `GET /market/klines`, `GET /market/data-coverage`, paging, cache coverage, drift alarm.
- Per case: id (`E08-TC-<group><nn>`), preconditions (named fixture from the `E08-T05` corpus + symbol + env), steps, expected observable result, the `US-MKT-*` id and child ticket it verifies, and automation status (`E08-Q02`/`E08-Q05` or manual-only).
- **Fixture/test-data appendix**: which corpus fixture drives which case — clean BTCUSDT/ETHUSDT window, mid-cap window, sequence-gap window, reconnect window, ticker delta-only burst, kline page-boundary set, `10018`/`10002`/5xx error payloads, `instruments-info` payload with a delisted symbol and a changed tick size.
- **Oracle definitions**: for every "is the data correct?" case, the plan names the independent oracle — REST `GET /v5/market/orderbook` snapshot diff for the book, `GET /v5/market/recent-trade` for the tape, exchange-side kline rows for backfill — rather than comparing the system to itself.
- **Traceability table** US-MKT-001..009 × test case × automation status, in the conventions of `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`, proving no story is untested.
- **Defect conventions for this epic**: any case where data is wrong *without a visible staleness/desync signal* is `priority/p0-critical` by definition; a visible-and-honest degradation is at most P2.

## Out of scope
- Writing the automation (`E08-Q02` integration/contract pack, `E08-Q05` E2E + a11y).
- Chaos scenarios (`E08-Q03`) and performance/load scripts (`E08-Q04`).
- Exploratory charters, epic regression pack and sign-off (`E08-Q06`).
- Security-owned artefacts: STRIDE (`E08-X01`), abuse cases (`E08-X02`), SAST/DAST rules (`E08-X03`).
- Anything consuming this data downstream: bar builders (E12), footprint/profiles (E22/E24), WS gateway framing (E17), OMS (E29).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every MKT story is covered by an executable case
  Given the plan is merged at qa/plans/e08-market-data-test-plan.md
  When the traceability table is checked against US-MKT-001 through US-MKT-009
  Then every story id maps to at least one case with preconditions, steps and an expected result
  And every case names the fixture it needs and the child ticket it covers

Scenario: A case is executable by an engineer who did not write it
  Given a QA engineer with a staging URL, the E08-T05 fixture corpus and no other context
  When they execute group 5 (order-book reconstruction) end to end
  Then every step resolves to an unambiguous observable outcome via REST, WS or a metric
  And no step requires reading backend source to decide pass or fail

Scenario: Failure case - silent book divergence must be catchable
  Given case E08-TC-E06 replays the sequence-gap fixture
  When the book is compared against an independent REST snapshot oracle after resync
  Then the plan requires a top-50-level price/size equality assertion
  And a divergence with no DESYNCED state having been published is recorded as a P0 defect

Scenario: Edge case - instrument metadata changes under a live chart
  Given the instruments-info fixture that changes BTCUSDT tick size between refreshes
  When case E08-TC-A08 forces a catalogue refresh
  Then the plan requires a new instrument_versions row, a bumped metadata_version and re-validated rounding on the client
  And stale client-side rounding is recorded as a P1 defect against US-MKT-004

Scenario: Non-automatable cases are declared, not hidden
  Given a case that requires a real 12-hour catalogue refresh window
  When the plan marks it manual-only
  Then it states the manual execution cadence and links the follow-up automation Task
  And it is not silently counted as automated coverage in the traceability table
```

## Technical notes / design
- The plan is written against fixtures, not live Bybit, so it is deterministic and consumes no rate-limit budget (`docs/plan/06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §7.3). Live/demo execution is a separate, explicitly-marked smoke subset owned by `E08-T05`.
- Group ordering matches dependency order so a partially-implemented staging build can still run groups 1-3.
- Cases must assert on **internal vocabulary only** (principle P3, `docs/plan/20-architecture.md` §0): a case that asserts a Bybit field name outside the adapter is itself a defect in the plan.
- Where the observable is a metric, the case names the exact metric and label set from `E08-T06`'s registry rather than "check the dashboard".

## Test plan
- Peer review by the second QA/SDET plus the E08 tech lead; review checklist: every case has an oracle, every case names a fixture, no case depends on wall-clock luck.
- Dry-run execution of one case per group against the current staging build; unexecutable steps are rewritten, not waived.
- The traceability table is generated/checked by a small script so it cannot silently drift from the case list.

## Security notes
- No credential appears in the plan or in any fixture reference; fixtures are pre-redacted by `E08-T05`'s capture tool and the plan restates that requirement.
- Cases that probe error-message content must assert that upstream exchange error bodies are not echoed verbatim to clients (deferred detail to `E08-X02`).

## Accessibility notes
- Group 3 and group 1 cases that touch `SCR-100..104`, `SCR-041` and `SCR-152` must state the keyboard-only path alongside the pointer path; the full audit lives in `E08-Q05`.
- Any case whose expected result is "the value turns red" must also state the non-colour signal (text, icon, `aria-live` announcement) per `docs/plan/05-accessibility-standard.md`.

## Performance notes
- The plan references but does not duplicate the budgets in `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §2 (#3 tick→screen, #5 ingestion throughput, #6 backend-internal, #8 memory/symbol); numeric assertions live in `E08-Q04`.
- Functional cases must be runnable inside a normal CI window; anything needing >10 minutes is tagged and routed to the nightly pack.

## Observability
- Each group lists the metrics and log events that should move while it executes (`ingest_events_total`, `bus_subscriber_lag`, `book_resync_total`, `clock_drift_seconds`, connection-state gauges), so a silent no-op implementation fails the case.
- Plan execution results are recorded in the QA run log referenced by `E08-Q06`.

## Definition of Done
- Plan merged, reviewed by a second QA engineer and the E08 tech lead.
- Traceability table complete for US-MKT-001..009 with zero uncovered stories.
- One case per group dry-run executed and the results recorded on the ticket.
- Automation split agreed and reflected in `E08-Q02`, `E08-Q03`, `E08-Q04`, `E08-Q05` scope.
- Linked from `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`.

## Dependencies
- `E08-T01` (ports/error taxonomy define the observable error vocabulary), `E08-S01` (catalogue endpoints), `E08-T04` (WS ingestion skeleton) must exist in at least contract form.
- Fixture corpus `E08-T05` is required for execution but not for authoring; authoring may proceed against the fixture manifest.

## Branch
`chore/e08-qa-test-plan`

## References
- `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 (test plan per feature, white-box review, defect severity)
- `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 (QA sign-off), §2.2 (epic-level QA)
- `docs/plan/11-user-stories.md` US-MKT-001..009
- `docs/plan/22-api-openapi.yaml` `/instruments*`, `/market/klines`, `/market/trades`, `/market/orderbook`, `/market/data-coverage`
- `docs/plan/23-ws-protocol.md` §6.1 topic catalogue
- `docs/plan/14-screens-catalogue.md` SCR-041, SCR-100..104, SCR-152
- `docs/plan/18-traceability-matrix.md`


## Agent execution brief

**Read first**
1. `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md` §11 (test plan per feature, white-box review, defect severity)
2. `docs/plan/02-definition-of-ready-done.md` §3.2 (QA sign-off), §2.2 (epic-level QA)

title: Contract & integration test pack for the adapter against recorded Bybit fixtures
body:
## Context
Adapter rule 5 (`docs/plan/24-internal-schemas.md` §14.2) is binding: every adapter ships a contract-test suite run against recorded fixtures plus an opt-in live smoke test. `E08-T05` builds the corpus and the replay harness; this ticket builds the **executable pack** that turns the black-box plan (`E08-Q01`) groups 1-6 into automated tests, and turns **R6 Feed rot** from an incident into a CI failure.

The distinction from the engineering tickets' own unit tests matters: those test each module's internals. This pack tests the *boundary* — raw recorded Bybit frames in, internal domain events and public REST/WS payloads out — so it stays valid across the refactors E17 will impose when the WS gateway is built on top.

## Scope / Deliverables
- `services/api/tests/contract/bybit/` — **adapter contract tests**, one module per stream, each feeding raw fixture frames through the real adapter and asserting the normalised event:
  - `publicTrade` → `TradeEvent` (side, price/qty as `Decimal`, ms→µs timestamp, trade id, block-trade flag).
  - `orderbook.200` snapshot/delta → `BookSnapshot`/`BookDelta` with `u`/`seq` monotonicity, zero-size deletes, and depth truncation.
  - `tickers` full vs delta frames → `TickerEvent` with correct merge of partial payloads.
  - `kline` list-of-lists (descending) → ascending `KlineEvent` with `end = start + interval_ms - 1` and `confirm → confirmed`.
  - `instruments-info` → `Instrument` incl. every filter field of `24-internal-schemas.md` §2.
  - Error payloads `10018`, `10002`, `10001`, 5xx and HTML error pages → the internal taxonomy of `E08-T01`.
- **Schema-drift / feed-rot guard**: a test that asserts the *set* of fields present in each fixture payload equals a checked-in expected-field manifest, failing loudly with a diff when Bybit adds, renames or removes a field — plus a documented triage procedure (update manifest + adapter, or file a defect).
- **Round-trip invariants** (property-based, Hypothesis): replaying any book fixture and then applying an independent REST snapshot produces identical top-N levels; replaying a trade fixture twice is idempotent; kline paging over arbitrary split points reconstructs the same series as a single call.
- `services/api/tests/integration/ingestion/` — **pipeline integration tests** over the `E08-T05` replay harness: fixture → ConnectionManager → bus → book/bar state → REST/WS read surface, asserting `GET /market/orderbook`, `GET /market/trades`, `GET /market/klines`, `GET /market/data-coverage` and the WS topics `book.{symbol}.{depth}`, `trades.{symbol}`, `ticker.{symbol}` match the plan's expected results.
- **OpenAPI/WS contract assertions**: every response asserted against the schemas in `22-api-openapi.yaml` and the JSON Schemas of `23-ws-protocol.md` §13-15 via the shared validator from E02's codegen pipeline — no hand-written duplicate expectations.
- **P3 leakage test**: a test that imports every module outside `candleviewer/exchange/bybit/` and asserts no Bybit-native field name appears in emitted payloads (complements the lint rule in `E08-X03`).
- CI wiring: the pack runs on every PR touching `exchange/`, `ingestion/` or `bus/`, and nightly in full; fixture-heavy cases are marked so the PR subset stays under the CI budget.

## Out of scope
- Building or refreshing the fixture corpus and capture tool (`E08-T05`).
- Live/demo connectivity smoke tests (`E08-T05`, run with `pytest -m exchange_smoke`).
- Chaos/failure-injection scenarios (`E08-Q03`) and load/soak (`E08-Q04`).
- Browser E2E and a11y (`E08-Q05`).
- Downstream consumers' own contract tests (E12, E17, E22).

## Acceptance criteria
```gherkin
Scenario: Every fixture in the corpus is exercised by at least one test
  Given the E08-T05 fixture manifest
  When the contract pack runs
  Then every manifest entry is referenced by at least one test id
  And an unreferenced fixture fails a coverage meta-test with its name

Scenario: A Bybit payload change fails CI instead of production
  Given a fixture is edited to add an unknown field and rename an existing one to a Bybit-side name
  When the feed-rot guard runs
  Then the test fails naming both the added and the renamed field
  And the failure message links the triage procedure in the pack README

Scenario: Failure case - a sequence gap must invalidate, never patch
  Given the sequence-gap fixture is replayed through the pipeline
  When the gap frame is processed
  Then the book state becomes DESYNCED, a resubscribe is issued and book_resync_total increments
  And no delta is applied across the gap, asserted by comparing against the REST snapshot oracle

Scenario: Edge case - kline page boundary
  Given the page-boundary kline fixture covering exactly 1000 and 1001 rows
  When fetch_klines pages across the boundary
  Then the reconstructed series has no duplicated or missing bar open time
  And the property test over arbitrary split points also passes

Scenario: Internal vocabulary never leaks
  Given the P3 leakage test
  When any module outside exchange/bybit/ emits an event or API payload
  Then no Bybit-native key name appears in the serialised output
  And a deliberate violation added in a scratch branch fails the test
```

## Technical notes / design
- Tests are authored against the **ports** of `E08-T01`, not concrete classes, so a second exchange adapter can reuse the same contract suite verbatim — that reuse is the point of adapter rule 5.
- Time is injected (frozen clock helper) so kline boundaries, staleness and clock-sync cases are deterministic.
- Fixture replay runs at accelerated speed for CI; the 1x path is exercised only in the nightly soak (`E08-Q04`).
- Expected-field manifests live next to the fixtures and are reviewed by CODEOWNERS for `exchange/` so a silent manifest update cannot slip through.

## Test plan
- Self-verifying: the pack is its own deliverable. Verification is done by **mutation**: deliberately break the delta-merge, the descending-kline reversal, the zero-size delete handling and the `confirm` flag, and confirm a distinct test fails for each.
- Coverage: the pack contributes to the ≥85% backend threshold of `02-definition-of-ready-done.md`; the `exchange/bybit/` package must reach ≥90% because it is the only place Bybit semantics live.
- Runtime budget measured and recorded; PR subset ≤ 4 minutes.

## Security notes
- A CI check asserts no fixture contains anything matching the secret patterns (API keys, signatures, `X-BAPI-*` headers, account ids); this test fails the build rather than warning.
- Error-mapping tests assert the internal error carries a sanitised message and that upstream bodies are logged at debug with redaction, never surfaced to a client payload.
- Fixtures are treated as untrusted input: parser tests include malformed JSON, truncated frames, oversized payloads and unexpected types to prove the adapter rejects rather than crashes.

## Accessibility notes
- N/A — no UI surface in this pack. UI verification is `E08-Q05`. Stated explicitly per the DoR "N/A must be justified" rule.

## Performance notes
- Replay throughput of the harness is asserted to exceed 10x real-time so the nightly full-corpus run completes inside its window.
- The pack records per-stream parse time and fails if median parse exceeds the ≤3 ms budget of `06-performance-and-load-standard.md` §4 for the representative frame set (a smoke-level guard; the real numbers come from `E08-Q04`).

## Observability
- Integration tests assert the metric registry of `E08-T06` actually moves: `ingest_events_total`, `ingest_lag_seconds`, `book_resync_total`, `bus_queue_depth`, connection-state gauges.
- A test asserts every mapped error emits a structured log with the internal error code and no secret material.

## Definition of Done
- Pack merged, green in CI on PR subset and nightly full run.
- Mutation checks executed and recorded on the ticket (one deliberate break per invariant, each caught).
- Every `E08-Q01` case marked "automated" is genuinely automated and cross-linked by id.
- Feed-rot triage procedure documented in the pack README and linked from `docs/plan/03-testing-strategy.md`.
- Coverage gate green; `exchange/bybit/` ≥ 90%.

## Dependencies
- `E08-Q01` defines the cases; `E08-T05` provides corpus + harness; `E08-S05`/`E08-S06` provide book and backfill behaviour to assert.
- E02 codegen pipeline supplies the shared OpenAPI/WS schema validator.
